questions.stem: Boston Globe reporter Chris Reidy notes that the situation will improve only when there are ___ programs that address the many needs of the homeless .
questions.analysis:
【答案解析】

考查近义形容词辨析。根据空格中被修饰的成分所在的句子：Boston Globe reporter Chris Reidy notes that the situation will improve only when there areprograms that address the many needs of the homeless.不难发现，定语从句中有个关键短语many needs of homeless（无家可归者的许多需求），给解本题一个很好的提示，肯定要填一个与many相关的同义词汇。因此，根据同义替换和同义转述原则，[B]comprehensive表示“综合的，全面的”，选为本题的正确答案。其它选项：complex（复杂的）；complementary（补充的，互补的）；compensating（补偿的），也都是核心高频词汇，必须掌握。
questions.tips:
这道题考的是几个意思相近的形容词怎么区分。我们先别急着看选项，而是回到原文句子中找线索。原句说：“《波士顿环球报》记者Chris Reidy指出，只有当出现能够应对无家可归者多种需求的项目时，情况才会好转。”这里的关键词是“many needs”（多种需求）——也就是说，这些项目得覆盖方方面面，不能只解决一个问题。

既然要回应“多种需求”，那空格里填的词就得体现出“全面、覆盖广”的意思。四个选项里，comprehensive 正好就是这个意思，表示“综合的、全面的”，和“many needs”形成逻辑上的呼应。其他几个词虽然看起来也挺高级，但意思对不上：complex 是“复杂的”，强调难懂或结构繁复；complementary 指的是“互补的”，比如两样东西互相补充；compensating 则是“补偿性的”，比如弥补损失。这些都跟“满足多方面需求”没关系。

所以，解这类题的关键不是死记单词，而是结合上下文找语义匹配。看到“many needs”，就该想到需要一个表达“全面覆盖”的词，而不是被其他看似高大上的干扰项带偏。

【答案解析】

本题所在当句译为：“正如某人所说”，空格处应该选填[C]As。这是一个固定句型，as的用法：as sb puts it正如某人所说。
questions.tips:
这道题考查的是一个很常见的英语表达习惯。句子开头说“正如某人所说……”，这里需要一个能引导这种说法的词。

在英语里，“as” 就经常用来引出别人说过的话或普遍的看法，比如 “as he said”（正如他说的）、“as the old saying goes”（俗话说）等等。所以这里填 “As” 最自然、最地道。

其他选项虽然也能在某些语境下使用，但只有 “As” 能直接搭配 “put it” 构成固定说法 “as someone puts it”，意思是“正如某人所说的那样”。这个短语在考研阅读中出现频率很高，建议大家记住。

questions.stem: One of the federal government’s studies 9 that the number of the homeless will reach nearly ___ million by the end of this decade .
questions.analysis:
【答案解析】

文章最后的直接引语为Edward Zlotkowski所表达的具体内容，因此空格处所填词应有“说、表达”之意，A选项puts带入文中，as sb. puts it，译为“正如...所说”，为固定搭配，故A选项正确。B选项interprets（解释、说明）和C选项assume（假设，设想）都可以用来表达观点，但是不能与as sb....it形成固定搭配，且与原文语义不符，故排除。D选项makes词义丰富，若放入文中，make it 表示事业上获得成功或准时赶到等含义，不符合原文语义，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解句子结构和固定搭配。空格后面紧跟着“as...it”这样的结构，而前面又引用了Edward Zlotkowski的一段话，说明这里是在引述他本人的说法。

在英语中，当我们想表示“正如某人所说”时，最地道、最常见的表达就是as someone puts it。这里的“puts”不是“放置”的意思，而是“表达、说出”的一种习惯用法。所以选项A完全符合这个语境。

再来看其他选项：B选项“interprets”意思是“解释”，虽然也能接观点，但它强调的是对内容的理解和转述，而不是原话引用，而且不能和“as...it”搭配使用；C选项“assumes”是“假设”，明显不符合上下文——这里不是在猜测，而是在直接引用；D选项“makes”虽然有很多意思，但“make it”通常指“成功”或“及时到达”，放在这里语义完全不通。

因此，只有A选项既能满足语法搭配，又能准确传达“正如他所说”的意思，是最合适的答案。

表面上看起来是一道近形名词辨析题，但是在深层次却是考查上下文之间的衔接关系。第17题提到comprehensive programs that address the many needs of the homeless，许多项目和全面的项目之间必须进行协调，才能更好和发挥作用，因此选择[D]coordination（协调）。另外，supervision（监督，管理）；manipulation（操作，处理）；regulation（管理，调节，规定）。
questions.tips:

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text1
questions.article:
In spite of “ endless talk of difference ,” American society is an amazing machine for homogenizing people . There is “ the democratizing uniformity of dress and discourse , and the casualness and absence of deference ” characteristic of popular culture . People are absorbed into “ a culture of consumption ” launched by the 19th-century department stores that offered “ vast arrays of goods in an elegant atmosphere .” Instead of intimate shops catering to a knowledgeable elite, these were stores “anyone could enter, regardless of class or background." This turned shopping into a public and democratic act . The mass media, advertising and sports are other forces for homogenization .

Immigrants are quickly fitting into this common culture , which may not be altogether elevating but is hardly poisonous . Writing for the National Immigration Forum , Gregory Rodriguez reports that today ’s immigration is neither at unprecedented levels nor resistant to assimilation . In 1998 immigrants were 9.8 percent of population ; in 1900 , 13.6 percent . In the 10 years prior to 1990 , 3.1 immigrants arrived for every 1,000 residents ; in the 10 years prior to 1890 , 9.2 for every 1,000 . Now , consider three indices of assimilation — language , home ownership and intermarriage .

The 1990 Census revealed that “ a majority of immigrants from each of the fifteen most common countries of origin spoke English “ well ” or “ very well ” after ten years of residence .” The children of immigrants tend to be bilingual and proficient in English . “ By the third generation, the original language is lost in the majority of immigrant families .” Hence the description of America as a “ graveyard ” for language . By 1996 foreign-born immigrants who had arrived before 1970 had a home ownership rate of 75.6 percent , higher than the 69.8 percent rate among native-born Americans .

Foreign-born Asians and Hispanics “ have higher rates of intermarriage than do U.S-born whites and blacks .” By the third generation , one third of Hispanic women are married to non-Hispanics , and 41 percent of Asian-American women are married to non-Asians .

Rodriguez notes that children in remote villages around the world are fans of superstars like Arnold Schwarzenegger and Garth Brooks, yet “ some Americans fear that immigrants living within the United States remain somehow immune to the nation ’s assimilative power .”

Are there divisive issues and pockets of seething anger in America Indeed . It is big enough to have a bit of everything . But particularly when viewed against America ’s turbulent past, today ’s social indices hardly suggest a dark and deteriorating social environment.
questions.stem: The word “homogenizing” (Line 2, Para. 1) most probably means______ .
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. identifying    识别

B. associating    联想

C. assimilating    同化

D. monopolizing     垄断


【定位及答案】

句首的介词短语“In spite of”表示让步，说明它所引导的部分和主句之间存在转折关系。既然它所在的部分表明的是“不断地谈论差异”，那么homogenizing所在部分就应该说明美国社会是没有差异的社会。因此，homogenizing应和前文中的difference形成对照。此外，在2段2、5句中，作者使用了assimilation，这与一段中的homogenizing及homogenization相呼应。综上所述，C选项“同化”为正确答案。其他选项均是无中生有，故予以排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解上下文的逻辑关系。文章开头提到，尽管人们总在强调美国社会中的各种差异（比如种族、文化等），但作者紧接着用了一个“in spite of”引导的让步状语，暗示实际情况可能恰恰相反——也就是说，美国社会其实在朝着减少差异、变得越来越相似的方向发展。

这里出现的关键词是“homogenizing”，它的字面意思是“使同质化”。要选出最贴切的中文对应词，就得看哪个选项能准确表达“消除差异、趋于一致”这个意思。四个选项中，“识别”和“垄断”明显不沾边；“联想”虽然听起来有点抽象，但跟“消除差别”完全没关系。

而“同化”这个词，正好描述的是不同群体逐渐融合、变得相似的过程，比如移民慢慢接受主流文化，行为习惯趋同。而且后文还多次提到“assimilation”（同化），和这里的“homogenizing”形成明显的呼应。所以，正确答案只能是C选项。

做这类题时，别光盯着生词本身，一定要结合前后句的语气和逻辑。尤其是像“in spite of”“however”这种转折信号词，往往藏着解题的关键线索。

    因消费文化而出现


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的关键词he department stores of the 19th century定位至1段3句。由该句中的launched by可知19世纪的百货商店是“消费文化”的源头，而接下来的两句则说明这些商店是人人都能进入的，这使得购物变成了一种公众的、民主的行为。可见，购物已经成为了大众的消费文化，而19世纪的百货商店对大众的文化传播发挥了作用，故A选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【张冠李戴】B 成为大众消费者的温情小店：原文1段4句说19世纪的百货商店不是intimate shops，故排除。

【张冠李戴】C 满足了知识精英的需要：1段4句指明迎合知识精英的是以前的温情小店，可见C选项是“温情小店”的特点而非“百货商店”的特点，故排除。

【因果倒置】D 因消费文化而出现：该选项颠倒了因果关系，将“百货商店掀走起了消费文化运动”理解为“消费文化是百货商店出现的原因”，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是19世纪的百货商店起到了什么作用。我们要回到原文第一段去找线索。文中提到，这些百货商店是由“消费文化”推动而兴起的，并且特别强调了一个关键点：它们向所有人开放，不管你是谁，都可以进去逛、去买东西。

这就带来了一个重要的变化——购物不再只是少数人的特权，而变成了一种大众都能参与的公共活动。换句话说，百货商店让消费这件事变得“民主化”了，也让更多普通人接触并融入到一种新的生活方式和文化氛围中。

现在看选项，A选项说百货商店“在大众文化传播中发挥了作用”，这正好对应了原文的意思：它们通过开放的购物环境，把消费变成了一种流行文化现象，影响了更广泛的人群。

其他几个选项就不太靠谱了。B选项说它们是“温情小店”，但原文讲的是大型百货商场，不是小而温馨的店铺；C选项说只服务“知识精英”，可原文明明说“everyone was welcome”，显然不对；D选项说百货商店“因消费文化而出现”，看似合理，但原文用的是“launched the culture of consumption”，意思是百货商店**开创了**消费文化，而不是被消费文化催生的，因果关系搞反了。

所以，正确答案是A，因为它准确抓住了百货商店在推动大众文化普及方面的历史角色。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text1
questions.article:
In spite of “ endless talk of difference ,” American society is an amazing machine for homogenizing people . There is “ the democratizing uniformity of dress and discourse , and the casualness and absence of deference ” characteristic of popular culture . People are absorbed into “ a culture of consumption ” launched by the 19th-century department stores that offered “ vast arrays of goods in an elegant atmosphere .” Instead of intimate shops catering to a knowledgeable elite, these were stores “anyone could enter, regardless of class or background." This turned shopping into a public and democratic act . The mass media, advertising and sports are other forces for homogenization .

Immigrants are quickly fitting into this common culture , which may not be altogether elevating but is hardly poisonous . Writing for the National Immigration Forum , Gregory Rodriguez reports that today ’s immigration is neither at unprecedented levels nor resistant to assimilation . In 1998 immigrants were 9.8 percent of population ; in 1900 , 13.6 percent . In the 10 years prior to 1990 , 3.1 immigrants arrived for every 1,000 residents ; in the 10 years prior to 1890 , 9.2 for every 1,000 . Now , consider three indices of assimilation — language , home ownership and intermarriage .

The 1990 Census revealed that “ a majority of immigrants from each of the fifteen most common countries of origin spoke English “ well ” or “ very well ” after ten years of residence .” The children of immigrants tend to be bilingual and proficient in English . “ By the third generation, the original language is lost in the majority of immigrant families .” Hence the description of America as a “ graveyard ” for language . By 1996 foreign-born immigrants who had arrived before 1970 had a home ownership rate of 75.6 percent , higher than the 69.8 percent rate among native-born Americans .

Foreign-born Asians and Hispanics “ have higher rates of intermarriage than do U.S-born whites and blacks .” By the third generation , one third of Hispanic women are married to non-Hispanics , and 41 percent of Asian-American women are married to non-Asians .

Rodriguez notes that children in remote villages around the world are fans of superstars like Arnold Schwarzenegger and Garth Brooks, yet “ some Americans fear that immigrants living within the United States remain somehow immune to the nation ’s assimilative power .”

Are there divisive issues and pockets of seething anger in America Indeed . It is big enough to have a bit of everything . But particularly when viewed against America ’s turbulent past, today ’s social indices hardly suggest a dark and deteriorating social environment.
questions.stem: The text suggests that immigrants now in the U .S______ .

options.label: B
options.text: exert a great influence on American culture

options.label: C
options.text: are hardly a threat to the common culture

options.label: D
options.text: constitute the majority of the population

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. are resistant to homogenization

    排斥同化

B. exert a great influence on American culture

    对美国文化产生了重大影响

C. are hardly a threat to the common culture

    对大众文化几乎不是威胁

D. constitute the majority of the population

    占美国人口的绝大多数


【定位及答案】

本文的中心话题是美国移民问题。题干中的immigrants提供的信息不具体，所以要和选项中的关键词结合起来定位，C选项的hardly a threat和原文1段1句中的hardly poisonous意义相同。1句说到外来移民正在迅速适应大众文化，尽管其结果可能并未有整体的提升，但最起码也是无害的（hardly poisonous），接着2句说到当今的外来移民既没有处于空前水平，也不抗拒美国社会的同化，可见进入美国的移民对美国大众文化没有威胁可言，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 排斥同化：选项“排斥同化”与2段2句所提及的罗德里格斯的报告内容相反，该报告明确指出“移民不排斥同化”。实际上,这只是某些美国人的担心（五段后半句），故排除。

【反向干扰】B 对美国文化产生了重大影响：2段1句说的是移民正在适应大众文化且其结果是无害的，也就是说移民对美国文化影响不大，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 占美国人口的绝大多数：2段3、4句以一系列百分数说明移民的数量不多且呈下降趋势，绝非D选项所说的占绝大多数，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是关于移民对美国主流文化的影响。很多同学一看到“移民”就容易联想到文化冲突或者同化问题，但其实解题的关键在于回到原文第一段，看看作者到底说了什么。

文章开头就明确指出：新来的移民正在快速融入主流文化，虽然这种融合未必带来整体文化的提升，但至少是“无害的”（原文用的是 hardly poisonous）。紧接着第二句又强调，现在的移民数量并没有达到历史最高，而且他们并不抗拒被同化。这两句话合起来的意思很清晰：移民不仅没有破坏主流文化，反而在积极适应它。

再来看选项，C 项说移民“对主流文化几乎不构成威胁”，这正好和原文“hardly poisonous”以及“不抗拒同化”的意思吻合。换句话说，作者认为移民不是文化入侵者，而是在慢慢融入，所以谈不上威胁。

其他几个选项为什么不对呢？A 项说移民“排斥同化”，但原文明明说他们“不抗拒同化”，直接矛盾；B 项说移民“对美国文化影响巨大”，但文章强调的是他们被主流文化影响，而不是反过来主导文化；D 项提到移民“占人口大多数”，原文根本没提具体比例，纯属无中生有。

所以，正确答案是 C。做这类题时，一定要紧扣原文用词和语气，别被自己的常识或刻板印象带偏了方向。

questions.stem: Why are Arnold Schwarzenegger and Garth Brooks mentioned in Paragraph 5?

options.label: A
options.text: To prove their popularity around the world

options.label: B
options.text: To reveal the public's fear of immigrants

options.label: C
options.text: To give examples of successful immigrants

options.label: D
options.text: To show the powerful influence of American culture

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. To prove their popularity  around the world

   证明他们在全世界都深受喜爱

B. To reveal the public's fear of immigrants

   为了显示公众为外来移民的担心

C. To give examples of successful immigrants

   为了给出外来移民获得成功的例子

D. To show the powerful influence of American culture

   说明美国文化强大的影响力


【定位及答案】

题干已定位至5段。该段1句中的“like”是一个表示例证的语段特征标志词。所以作者提到二人是为了论证children in remote villages around the world are fans of superstars（世界各地的偏远乡村的孩子们都是这样的超级巨星的影迷或歌迷）这一观点。紧接着该句的后半句说到，仍有美国人担心自已国家的同化力量对移民可能会不起作用，显然后半句是在暗示他们的这种担心是多余的，因为美国文化的影响力非常强大，故D选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【以例证例】A 证明他们在全世界都深受喜爱：选项是例子本身，如果说原文用二人深受欢迎的事例来证明他们深受喜爱，那就犯了“同一概念证明自己”的错误，这是无法表明例证关系的，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 为了显示公众为外来移民的担心：5段yet前后是转折关系，而非因果关系，况且这只是某些美国人的担心，而非所有公众的担心，故排除。

【无中生有】C 为了给出外来移民获得成功的例子：作者引用此二人事例，是为了说明成功的美国文化，而非成功的移民，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是作者为什么在第五段提到那两位名人。很多同学一看到“提到某人”，就下意识觉得是在夸他们多厉害或多受欢迎，但其实关键要看上下文——作者用这个例子到底想说明什么。

我们回到原文第五段开头：“Even children in remote villages around the world are fans of superstars like Arnold Schwarzenegger and Garth Brooks...” 这句话的重点不在施瓦辛格或布鲁克斯本人，而在于“连偏远村庄的孩子都知道他们”。这里的“like”明显是在举例子，用来支撑前面那个更宏观的观点：美国流行文化已经渗透到全球各个角落。

紧接着，句子后半部分说“yet some Americans worry that their country’s assimilative power may be failing”。注意这个“yet”——它表示转折。意思是：明明全世界都在追美国明星、受美国文化影响，可还有些美国人却担心自己的文化“同化力”不够强。作者其实在暗讽这种担心是多余的，因为现实恰恰证明了美国文化的影响力非常强大。

所以，提到这两位明星，根本目的不是为了夸他们个人（排除A），也不是为了聚焦公众对移民的恐惧（B选项把次要信息当成了主旨），更不是单纯展示移民的成功故事（C偏离了文化影响力的主线）。作者真正想说的是：你看，连最偏远的地方都逃不开美国文化的影响，还担心啥同化不了？因此，D选项才准确抓住了作者的意图。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text1
questions.article:
In spite of “ endless talk of difference ,” American society is an amazing machine for homogenizing people . Now , consider three indices of assimilation — language , home ownership and intermarriage .

The 1990 Census revealed that “ a majority of immigrants from each of the fifteen most common countries of origin spoke English “ well ” or “ very well ” after ten years of residence .” The children of immigrants tend to be bilingual and proficient in English . “ By the third generation, the original language is lost in the majority of immigrant families .” Hence the description of America as a “ graveyard ” for language . Foreign-born Asians and Hispanics “ have higher rates of intermarriage than do U.S-born whites and blacks .” By the third generation , one third of Hispanic women are married to non-Hispanics , and 41 percent of Asian-American women are married to non-Asians .

Are there divisive issues and pockets of seething anger in America Indeed . It is big enough to have a bit of everything . But particularly when viewed against America ’s turbulent past, today ’s social indices hardly suggest a dark and deteriorating social environment.
questions.stem: In the author’s opinion, the absorption of immigrants into American society is_____ .
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. rewarding     值得的

B. Successful     成功的

C. Fruitless     无用的

D. harmful     有害的


【定位及答案】

做观点态度题时，首先可以从作者使用的词汇来体会其态度。对吸收外来移民进入美国社会这一事件，作者在1段1句、2段1句、6段4句分别用了amazing, quickly fitting into, hardly poisonous, hardly suggest a dark and deteriorating social environment等词汇来描述，不难看出作者的态度是肯定的。即作者认为，美国社会吸收外来移民发挥了积极的作用，据此可直接排除C、D两个选项【反向干扰】。A选项rewarding和B选项successful表达的都是正面肯定意义，但successful强调“成功的，结果良好的”，而rewarding则强调“有好处，值得去做”。从文章中看不出美国社会吸纳移民希望得到什么具体的报答，因此排除A选项，正确答案是B选项。
questions.tips:
这道题考查的是作者对美国吸纳外来移民这件事持什么态度。要判断作者的态度，关键不是靠自己的主观想法，而是回到文章里找线索——尤其是作者用了哪些带有感情色彩的词。

比如，文章开头就说这种融合现象“amazing”（令人惊叹），后面又提到新移民“quickly fitting into”（很快融入）美国社会，还特别强调这种融合“hardly poisonous”（几乎无害），甚至说根本看不出社会环境因此变得“dark and deteriorating”（黑暗和恶化）。这些用词都明显带着赞赏和肯定的语气，说明作者认为这件事整体上是积极、正面的。

有了这个基调，我们就可以先把明显负面的选项排除掉。C项“fruitless”（徒劳无功）和D项“harmful”（有害）显然和作者的立场相悖，直接出局。

剩下A项“rewarding”和B项“successful”看起来都是褒义词，但意思有细微差别。“Rewarding”强调的是“有回报、值得投入”，通常暗含一种付出后获得收益的感觉；而“successful”更侧重事情本身达成了良好结果。通读全文，作者并没有说美国吸收移民是为了图什么回报，而是反复强调融合过程顺利、社会没有因此崩溃，甚至运转得不错——这更符合“成功”（successful）的含义，而不是“值得”（rewarding）。

所以，正确答案是B，因为它最准确地反映了作者对这一社会现象的整体评价：融合不仅没出问题，反而进行得很顺利、很成功。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text2
questions.article:
Stratford-on-Avon , as we all know , has only one industry — William Shakespeare — but there are two distinctly separate and increasingly hostile branches . There is the Royal Shakespeare Company ( RSC ) ,which presents superb productions of the plays at the Shakespeare Memorial Theatre on the Avon . And there are the townsfolk who largely live off the tourists who come , not to see the plays , but to look at Anne Hathaway ’s Cottage, Shakespeare ’s birthplace and the other sights .

The worthy residents of Stratford doubt that the theatre adds a penny to their revenue . They frankly dislike the RSC ’s actors , them with their long hair and beards and sandals and noisiness . It’s all deliciously ironic when you consider that Shakespeare , who earns their living , was himself an actor ( with a beard ) and did his share of noise-making .

The tourist streams are not entirely separate . The sightseers who come by bus — and often take in Warwick Castle and Blenheim Palace on the side — don’t usually see the plays , and some of them are even surprised to find a theatre in Stratford . However, the playgoers do manage a little sight-seeing along with their playgoing . It is the playgoers, the RSC contends , who bring in much of the town ’ s revenue because they spend the night ( some of them four or five nights ) pouring cash into the hotels and restaurants . The sightseers can take in everything and get out of town by nightfall .

The townsfolk don’t see it this way and the local council does not contribute directly to the subsidy of the Royal Shakespeare Company . Stratford cries poor traditionally . Nevertheless every hotel in town seems to be adding a new wing or cocktail lounge . Hilton is building its own hotel there , which you may be sure will be decorated with Hamlet Hamburger Bars , the Lear Lounge , the Banquo Banqueting Room , and so forth , and will be very expensive .

Anyway , the townsfolk can’t understand why the Royal Shakespeare Company needs a subsidy . ( The theatre has broken attendance records for three years in a row . Last year its 1,431 seats were 94 percent occupied all year long and this year they ’ll do better .) The reason , of course , is that costs have rocketed and ticket prices have stayed low .

It would be a shame to raise prices too much because it would drive away the young people who are Stratford ’s most attractive clientele . They come entirely for the plays , not the sights . They all seem to look alike ( though they come from all over ) — lean , pointed , dedicated faces , wearing jeans and sandals , eating their buns and bedding down for the night on the flagstones outside the theatre to buy the 20 seats and 80 standing-room tickets held for the sleepers and sold to them when the box office opens at 10:30 a.m .
questions.stem: From the first two paragraphs, we learn that______ .

options.label: A
options.text: the townsfolk deny the RSC’s contribution to the town’s revenue

options.label: B
options.text: the actors of the RSC imitate Shakespeare on and off stage

options.label: C
options.text: the two branches of the RSC are not on good terms

options.label: D
options.text: the townsfolk earn little from tourism

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. the townsfolk deny the RSC’s contribution to the town’s revenue

    小镇居民否定RSC对小镇收入的贡献

B. the actors of the RSC imitate Shakespeare on and off stage

    RSC的演员在台上台下模仿莎士比亚

C. the two branches of the RSC are not on good terms

    RSC的两个分支关系不友好

D. the townsfolk earn little from tourism

    镇上居民从旅游业中赚钱很少


【定位及答案】

题干已经定位在前两段。2段1句说：斯特拉特福德镇的居民认为剧院一点也没有增加他们的收入，也就是说，小镇居民否认剧院对其收入有贡献。A选项中的deny是对原文中doubt的同义转述，contribution to与原文中adds a penny to表意相同，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】B RSC的演员在台上台下模仿莎士比亚：2段2、3句说的是“演员们在演莎士比亚的剧作”，而B选项说的是“演员们在台上台下模仿莎士比亚本人”，两者表达的含义不同，故排除。

【偷换概念】C RSC的两个分支关系不友好：原文所提及的两个分支指的是小镇产业的两个分支，并非C选项所涉及的RSC的两个分支，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 镇上居民从旅游业中赚钱很少：原文1段3句说的是小镇居民主要靠赚游客的钱过活，可见他们的收人主要来源于旅游业，D选项与此恰恰相反，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于准确理解文章前两段的意思，尤其是第二段开头那句话。作者提到，斯特拉特福德镇的居民“doubt that the theatre adds a penny to their revenue”，翻译过来就是：他们怀疑剧院有没有给他们的收入带来哪怕一丁点好处。换句话说，当地人并不认为皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）对小镇经济有什么实质帮助。

选项A说“小镇居民否定RSC对小镇收入的贡献”，这其实正是原文意思的自然转述。“doubt”在这里表达的是一种否定态度，虽然语气比“deny”稍微弱一点，但在考研英语的语境中，这种程度的同义替换是完全可以接受的。而且“adds a penny to their revenue”和“contribution to the town’s revenue”说的是一回事——都是指经济上的收益。

再来看其他几个选项，为什么不对呢？B选项提到演员在台下也模仿莎士比亚，但原文根本没讲演员私下的行为，完全是无中生有。C选项说RSC内部两个分支关系不好，文章里压根没提“两个分支”这回事，属于凭空捏造。D选项说居民从旅游业赚得少，听起来好像有点道理，但原文只是否定剧院带来的收入，并没有泛泛地说整个旅游业收益低——说不定游客多、酒店火、餐厅赚钱，只是这些钱跟剧院没关系而已。所以D扩大了范围，偷换了概念。

总的来说，做这类题要抓住原文的“核心态度”：居民对RSC的经济作用持怀疑甚至否定态度。只要紧扣这一点，就能轻松排除干扰项，选出最贴近原意的答案。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text2
questions.article:
Stratford-on-Avon , as we all know , has only one industry — William Shakespeare — but there are two distinctly separate and increasingly hostile branches . There is the Royal Shakespeare Company ( RSC ) ,which presents superb productions of the plays at the Shakespeare Memorial Theatre on the Avon . And there are the townsfolk who largely live off the tourists who come , not to see the plays , but to look at Anne Hathaway ’s Cottage, Shakespeare ’s birthplace and the other sights .

The worthy residents of Stratford doubt that the theatre adds a penny to their revenue . They frankly dislike the RSC ’s actors , them with their long hair and beards and sandals and noisiness . It’s all deliciously ironic when you consider that Shakespeare , who earns their living , was himself an actor ( with a beard ) and did his share of noise-making .

The tourist streams are not entirely separate . The sightseers who come by bus — and often take in Warwick Castle and Blenheim Palace on the side — don’t usually see the plays , and some of them are even surprised to find a theatre in Stratford . However, the playgoers do manage a little sight-seeing along with their playgoing . It is the playgoers, the RSC contends , who bring in much of the town ’ s revenue because they spend the night ( some of them four or five nights ) pouring cash into the hotels and restaurants . The sightseers can take in everything and get out of town by nightfall .

The townsfolk don’t see it this way and the local council does not contribute directly to the subsidy of the Royal Shakespeare Company . Stratford cries poor traditionally . Nevertheless every hotel in town seems to be adding a new wing or cocktail lounge . Hilton is building its own hotel there , which you may be sure will be decorated with Hamlet Hamburger Bars , the Lear Lounge , the Banquo Banqueting Room , and so forth , and will be very expensive .

Anyway , the townsfolk can’t understand why the Royal Shakespeare Company needs a subsidy . ( The theatre has broken attendance records for three years in a row . Last year its 1,431 seats were 94 percent occupied all year long and this year they ’ll do better .) The reason , of course , is that costs have rocketed and ticket prices have stayed low .

It would be a shame to raise prices too much because it would drive away the young people who are Stratford ’s most attractive clientele . They come entirely for the plays , not the sights . They all seem to look alike ( though they come from all over ) — lean , pointed , dedicated faces , wearing jeans and sandals , eating their buns and bedding down for the night on the flagstones outside the theatre to buy the 20 seats and 80 standing-room tickets held for the sleepers and sold to them when the box office opens at 10:30 a.m .
questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 3 that_____ .

options.label: A
options.text: The sightseers cannot visit the Castle and the Palace separately

options.label: B
options.text: the playgoers spend more money than the sightseers

options.label: C
options.text: the sightseers do more shopping than the playgoers

options.label: D
options.text: the playgoers go to no other places in town than the theater

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. The sightseers cannot visit the Castle and the Palace separately

    游客不能分别参观城保和宫殿

B.  the playgoers spend more money than the sightseers

    戏迷比游客花费更多

C.  the sightseers do more shopping than the playgoers

    游客比戏迷购物更多

D. the playgoers go to no other places in town than the theater

    除了剧院，戏迷不会去城里其他地方


【定位及答案】

题干已定位在3段。该段4、5句提到看戏的人给小镇带来了丰厚的收入,从细节上看，看戏的人要在镇上过夜，而观光的人一般当天就会离开了，可见，戏迷会比观光者支付更多的住宿费用和生活费用，他们比普通游客花费更多，因此B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【过度推理】A 游客不能分别参观城保和宫殿：原文3段2句提到，“观光者通常会去参观沃里克城堡和布伦海姆宫殿”，由此并不能推出这两个景点必须一起参观，故排除。

【无中生有】C 游客比戏迷购物更多：原文讲游客和戏迷做比较是为了说明二者的花费，但文中并没有提到购物，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 除了剧院，戏迷不会去城里其他地方：由3段3、4句来看，看戏的人会观光，还会在酒店和餐馆消费，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解第三段中对两类人——“看戏的人”（playgoers）和“观光客”（sightseers）——消费行为的对比。原文提到，看戏的人通常会在镇上过夜，而观光客则大多当天往返、不会留宿。

这意味着看戏的人不仅买票看演出，还要花钱住酒店、吃饭、可能还会买些纪念品，整体开销自然比只是白天来转一圈就走的游客要大得多。虽然文章没有直接说“戏迷花得更多”，但通过他们停留时间更长这个细节，完全可以合理推断出他们的总支出更高。

再来看选项：A 说游客不能分开参观城堡和宫殿，但原文根本没提这个限制；C 说游客购物更多，可文中没有任何关于购物多少的比较；D 说得太绝对了，说戏迷只去剧院不去别处，这明显过度推断。只有 B 选项“戏迷比游客花得更多”是能从文中信息合理推出的结论。

所以，正确答案是 B，因为它紧扣原文细节，并且符合逻辑推断，而不是靠主观猜测或夸大其词。做这类题时，一定要抓住“谁做了什么”“有什么不同”，然后看哪个选项最忠实于原文的意思。

questions.stem: By saying “Stratford cries poor traditionally ”(Line2-3, Para4), the author implies that_____ .

options.label: A
options.text: Stratford cannot afford the expansion projects

options.label: B
options.text: Stratford has long been in financial difficulties

options.label: C
options.text: the town is not really short of money

options.label: D
options.text: the townsfolk used to be poorly paid

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. Stratford cannot afford the expansion projects

    斯特拉特福德镇无力负担扩张的项目

B. Stratford has long been in financial difficulties

    斯特拉特福德镇已长期处于财政困难之中

C. the town is not really short of money

    实际上小镇很富有

D. the townsfolk used to be poorly paid

    小镇居民过去的工资很低


【定位及答案】

文章4段2句提及“cries poor”之后，在3句开头使用了转折连词Nevertheless，该词是对2句的引出，重点表达的应是3句的内容。3、4句说到小镇上的旅馆，包括希尔顿都想在那里筹建自己酒店，其中涉及到一些very expensive的东西，这种做法无非是想借助莎士比亚的名声来赚钱。显而易见，小镇并不缺钱，否则也不会有财力承担这一切花销。可见，哭穷只不过是一种传统罢了，因此C选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A、B两个选项为反向干扰，4段3、4句表明每家旅馆都在进行扩建，因此不太可能负担不起扩建的开支，也不太可能出现财政困难，故排除。

【无中生有】D 小镇居民过去的工资很低：选项原文未提，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于读懂作者的言外之意。文章第四段提到，斯特拉特福德镇“喊穷”（cries poor），但紧接着用了一个Nevertheless（然而）来转折——这个信号词特别重要，说明后面的内容才是重点。

接下来作者说，包括希尔顿在内的多家高档酒店都想在这个小镇建新项目，而且这些项目都“非常昂贵”（very expensive）。你想啊，如果一个地方真的穷得叮当响，怎么可能吸引这么多大公司砸钱搞豪华建设？更别说这些项目本身也需要当地有一定的经济基础和消费能力才能支撑起来。

所以，作者其实是在暗示：小镇根本不是没钱，所谓的“哭穷”只是一种说法、一种传统，甚至可能是为了争取更多政策支持或舆论同情。真正的情况恰恰相反——它有足够的财力和吸引力，才会让这么多高端品牌争着入驻。

选项C说“小镇实际上并不缺钱”，正好符合这个逻辑。而A和B说小镇财政困难或者负担不起扩张，明显和文中提到的大量投资事实相矛盾；D选项讲的是居民过去工资低，但原文压根没提工资问题，属于无中生有。因此，正确答案只能是C。

questions.stem: According to the townsfolk, the RSC deserves no subsidy because_____ .

options.label: A
options.text: ticket prices can be raised to cover the spending

options.label: C
options.text: the behavior of the actors is not socially acceptable

options.label: D
options.text: the theatre attendance is on the rise

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. ticket prices can be raised to cover the spending

    提高票价可以解决费用问题

B. the company is financially ill-managed

    剧团在财政方面管理不善

C. the behavior of the actors is not socially acceptable

    演员的行为没有得到社会认可

D. the theatre attendance is on the rise

    剧院的上座率持续上涨


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的关键词townsfolk和no subsidy定位在5段。5段2、3句是5段1句中can’t understand的原因；而4句明确提到的the reason是1句中needs的原因。两处表达的是两个不同的原因，而题干问的是can't understand的原因，所以答案就是五段括号中的两句话，即“剧场上座率不断提高”，因此D选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【张冠李戴】A 提高票价可以解决费用问题：5段4句是剧团认为的需要补助的原因，而6段1句虽然提到提高票价的问题，但这是为了说明提高票价所带来的后果，与RSC是否应该得到补贴无关，故排除。

【无中生有】B 剧团在财政方面管理不善：选项原文未提，故排除。

【无关干扰】C 演员的行为没有得到社会认可：2段2句提到小镇居民对演员的行为不满，这一点与财政问题无关，也不是题干所问原因，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于搞清楚题干到底在问什么。题目问的是“镇上居民（townsfolk）为什么不能理解剧团还需要补贴”，也就是说，我们要找的是他们感到困惑的原因，而不是剧团自己说的需要补贴的理由。

回到原文第五段，第一句话就点出：镇上的人不理解为什么这个剧团还需要政府补贴。接下来两句解释了他们的疑惑——因为最近来看戏的人越来越多，剧场几乎场场爆满。在普通人看来，既然观众这么多、生意这么好，那肯定不缺钱，自然就不该再要补贴了。所以，“上座率持续上涨”才是他们觉得“无法理解”的根本原因。

有些同学可能会被后面那句“剧团声称票价太低、入不敷出”带偏，以为这是重点。但注意，那是剧团自己的说法，不是镇上居民的想法。题干明确问的是“居民不理解的原因”，所以我们只看他们眼中的事实——人多、火爆、看起来很赚钱。这就对应选项D。

其他几个选项都站不住脚：A说的是“提高票价能解决问题”，但原文没提居民是否认为该涨价；B说剧团财政管理差，这完全是无中生有；C提到演员行为不得体，文章压根没涉及。只有D准确反映了居民所看到的现象，也就是他们产生疑问的依据。

questions.stem: From the text we can conclude that the author_____ .
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. is supportive of both sides

    对双方都予以支持

B. favors the townsfolk's view

    支持小镇居民的看法

C. takes a detached attitude

    持不偏不倚的态度

D. is sympathetic to the RSC

    同情RSC


【定位及答案】

题干中信息不够,要根据选项定位。纵观全文，作者对小镇居民不乏批评之言：小镇居民不喜欢RSC的演员，但却靠着莎士比亚的名气赚钱，很显然此处作者的态度是嘲讽的（2段2、3句）。小镇居民不理解RSC对小镇做出的贡献（3段），同时，还一边哭穷， 一边大肆扩建（4段），显然作者不支持居民的行为，所以A、B两个选项【反向干扰】错误。另方面：作者 处处为RSC说好话，说他们的演出是 superb production（1段2句），并具体描述了他们如何为小镇做贡献（3段4句），却得不到小镇居民的理解（4段1句)，虽然困难,却又不能提高票价（5段），6段1句中的a shame使作者同情的态度跃然纸上，故排除C选项【曲解文义】，故正确答案是D选项。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是作者对文中争议双方——小镇居民和皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）——持什么态度。要判断作者立场，不能光看表面，得仔细琢磨他字里行间流露出来的情绪。

先看作者怎么写小镇居民。文章第二段就点出一个矛盾：居民一边嫌弃RSC的演员“吵闹”“不体面”，一边又靠着莎士比亚的名气大把赚钱。这种“吃着碗里骂着锅里”的行为，作者显然觉得挺讽刺。到了第四段，作者更直接了——说居民嘴上喊穷，转头却花大钱扩建酒店，这种言行不一的做法，很难让人相信作者是在支持他们。

再看作者对RSC的态度。开篇第一段就夸他们的演出是“superb production”（精彩绝伦的制作），语气明显带着欣赏。后面几段还详细说明RSC为小镇带来了游客、活力甚至经济收益，可居民不但不领情，反而抱怨连连。更让人心疼的是，RSC明明处境艰难，却因为票价敏感不敢涨价，作者在第六段用了一句“a shame”（真可惜/真不公平），这句话虽然简短，但饱含同情，几乎等于直接表态了。

综合来看，作者既没有“两边都支持”，也没有“保持中立”，更不可能站在小镇居民那边。相反，他对RSC的困境感同身受，字里行间透着理解与惋惜。所以，正确答案是D：作者对RSC抱有同情之心。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text3
questions.article:
When prehistoric man arrived in new parts of the world , something strange happened to the large animals : they suddenly became extinct . Smaller species survived . The large , slow-growing animals were easy game , and were quickly hunted to extinction . Now something similar could be happening in the oceans .

That the seas are being overfished has been known for years . What researchers such as Ransom Myers and Boris Worm have shown is just how fast things are changing . They have looked at half a century of data from fisheries around the world . Their methods do not attempt to estimate the actual biomass ( the amount of living biological matter ) of fish species in particular parts of the ocean , but rather changes in that biomass over time . According to their latest paper published in Nature, the biomass of large predators ( animals that kill and eat other animals ) in a new fishery is reduced on average by 80% within 15 years of the start of exploitation . In some long-fished areas, it has halved again since then.

Dr. Worm acknowledges that these figures are conservative . One reason for this is that fishing technology has improved . Today 's vessels can find their prey using satellites and sonar , which were not available 50 years ago . That means a higher proportion of what is in the sea is being caught , so the real difference between present and past is likely to be worse than the one recorded by changes in catch sizes . In the early days , too , longlines would have been more saturated with fish . Some individuals would therefore not have been caught , since no baited hooks would have been available to trap them , leading to an underestimate of fish stocks in the past . Furthermore , in the early days of longline fishing , a lot of fish were lost to sharks after they had been hooked . That is no longer a problem , because there are fewer sharks around now .

Dr. Myers and Dr. Worm argue that their work gives a correct baseline , which future management efforts must take into account . They believe the data support an idea current among marine biologists , that of the " shifting baseline ". The notion is that people have failed to detect the massive changes which have happened in the ocean because they have been looking back only a relatively short time into the past . That matters because theory suggests that the maximum sustainable yield that can be cropped from a fishery comes when the biomass of a target species is about 50% of its original levels . Most fisheries are well below that , which is a bad way to do business .
questions.stem: The extinction of large prehistoric animals is noted to suggest that_____ .

options.label: A
options.text: large animals were vulnerable to the changing environment

options.label: B
options.text: small species survived as large animals disappeared

options.label: C
options.text: large sea animals may face the same threat today

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. large animals were vulnerable to the changing environment

    大型动物容易被变化的环境伤害

B. small species survived as large animals disappeared

    大型动物消失的时候小型动物幸存了下来

C. large sea animals may face the same threat today

    如今大型海洋动物会面临同样的威胁

D. Slow-growing fish outlive fast-growing ones

    缓慢生长的鱼类比快速生长的鱼类活得长


【定位及答案】

根据题干定位在1段。细读原文，不难发现，大型动物灭绝是一个例证， 目的是引出首段末句的话题：一些类似的情况可能正在海洋中发生，something similar（类似的情况）指上文1句和3句中的extinct 和extinction。C选项中的face the same threat 同义替换了1段4句中的something similar，因此C选项是正确答案。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 大型动物容易被变化的环境伤害：选项在原文并未提及，因此为错误选项。

【以例证例】B 大型动物消失的时候小型动物幸存了下来：选项是例证本身，无法论证观点，且根据首段2、3句所言，大型动物的灭亡与小型动物幸存之间并无必然联系，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 缓慢生长的鱼类比快速生长的鱼类活得长：由1段3、4句可知，生长慢的大型鱼类比较容易遭到猎捕，最终灭绝，但其与快速生长的鱼类谁活得更长，文章并未指出，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于搞清楚作者在第一段到底想说什么。开头提到史前大型动物灭绝了，但这并不是文章的重点，而是一个引子。真正重要的是最后一句话——“something similar may be happening in the oceans today”（类似的事情如今可能正在海洋中发生）。这句话才是作者写这一段的真正目的。

也就是说，前面讲陆地上大型动物因为环境变化而灭绝，是为了类比现在海洋里大型动物也可能面临同样的危险。所以正确选项必须体现出“现在海洋中的大型动物正在遭遇和过去陆地大型动物类似的威胁”这个意思。

看选项C：“large sea animals may face the same threat today”（如今大型海洋动物可能面临同样的威胁），正好精准对应原文最后一句的含义。“the same threat”指的就是前文提到的灭绝风险，这种同义转述非常自然，也完全符合作者的写作意图。

其他几个选项虽然看起来有点道理，但其实都偏离了重点。比如A选项说大型动物容易受环境变化影响，这虽然是事实，但只是背景信息，不是作者要强调的“现在海洋也在发生类似情况”这个核心观点。B选项提到小型动物存活下来，原文根本没讨论小动物的命运。D选项讲生长快慢和寿命的关系，更是无中生有，文章压根没提这一点。

所以，解这类题不能只盯着细节，而要抓住段落的写作目的——作者举过去的例子，是为了说明现在可能发生的问题。一旦你看出这个逻辑链条，答案就水到渠成了。

questions.stem: We can infer from Dr. Myers and Dr. Worm's paper that____ .

options.label: A
options.text: the stock of large predators in some old fisheries has reduced by 90%

options.label: B
options.text: there are only half as many fisheries as there were 15 years ago

options.label: C
options.text: the catch sizes in new fisheries are only 20% of the original amount

options.label: D
options.text: the number of larger predators dropped faster in new fisheries than in the old

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. the stock of large predators in some old fisheries has reduced by 90%

    一些旧渔场的大型食肉动物生物量减少了90%

B. there are only half as many fisheries as there were 15 years ago

    现在的渔场数量只有15年前渔场数量的一半

C. the catch sizes in new fisheries are only 20% of the original amount

    新渔场的捕捞规模只有过去的20%

D. the number of larger predators dropped faster in new fisheries than in the old

    新渔场大型食肉动物的数量下降得比旧渔场快


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Dr. Myers and Dr. Worm's paper定位在2段5、6句。由这两句可知,新渔场的鱼量先是下降了80% （注意：不是下降到80%），也就是剩下100%-80 =20%了；然后那些长期捕捞的渔场在此（20%）基础上又（注意：原文中的again）减少了一半，也就是说总共减少了80%+10%=90% ，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】原文根本没有论述渔场的数量，也没有论述捕捞规模，而论述的是食肉动物的生物量，因此B、C两个选项均错误。

【偷换概念】D 新渔场大型食肉动物的数量下降得比旧渔场快：根据上述讲解可知，新、旧两个渔场的鱼量分别下降了80%和90% ，从数字上看，旧渔场下降得更多，但文中并无信息显示这一结果是发生在相同的时间段内，因此无法比较二者下降速率快慢，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于准确理解原文中关于渔场鱼类数量变化的描述。题干提到的是Dr. Myers和Dr. Worm的研究，所以我们需要回到文章第二段去找相关信息。

原文说，当一个新的渔场刚开始被开发时，大型掠食性鱼类的数量会迅速下降80%，也就是说只剩下原来的20%。注意，这里是“下降了80%”，不是“剩下80%”，这个区别很重要。接着，文章又提到，在那些已经被长期捕捞的“老”渔场里，鱼类数量在已经只剩20%的基础上，又再减少了一半。一半的20%就是10%，所以最终只剩下10%，相当于总共减少了90%。

现在来看选项，A选项说“一些旧渔场的大型掠食者数量减少了90%”，这正好和我们刚才推算的结果一致。而其他选项呢？B选项讲的是渔场总数减少了一半，但原文根本没提渔场数量的变化；C选项说新渔场的捕捞量是原来的20%，但原文说的是鱼的数量剩下20%，不是捕捞量；D选项说新渔场的掠食者减少得更快，但原文其实强调的是老渔场在原有基础上进一步恶化，并没有比较“速度”谁快谁慢。

所以，正确答案是A。解这类题最怕的就是望文生义或者忽略关键词，比如“again”“half”这些词，它们往往藏着关键的计算逻辑。一定要沉住气，把数字关系理清楚，才能避开陷阱。

questions.stem: By saying “these figures are conservative” (Line 1, Para3), Dr. Worm means that_____ .

options.label: B
options.text: the catch-sizes are actually smaller than recorded

options.label: C
options.text: the marine biomass has suffered a greater loss

options.label: D
options.text: the data collected so far are out of date

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. fishing technology has improved rapidly

   捕鱼技术迅速提高了    

B. the catch-sizes are actually smaller than recorded

   那时的捕鱼规模实际上比记录的小

C. the marine biomass has suffered a greater loss

   海洋的生物量遭受了更大的损失

D. the data collected so far are out of date

   到目前为止所收集到的数据过时了


【定位及答案】

根据题干定位在3段。思路一：该段1到4句说：沃姆博上承认这些数据（即上段的“海洋大型食肉动物的生物量减少情况”）是保守的，其中的一个理由是捕鱼技术提高了，这意味着更多的海洋生物正在被捕获，就是说：“海洋生物量遭受了更大损失”，因此C选项正确。思路二：3段2句的“One reason for this”说明题干表示的应该是“捕鱼技术提高的结果”。3段的2、3句之间是举例关系，而4句开头的“That means”则说明3、4两句之同存在因果关系，因此可以得出结论：4句means之后的部分“a higher proportion of what is in the sea is being caught”就是“捕鱼技术提高的结果”，因此题干表示的是“更大比例的海洋生物正在遭受捕杀”，C选项是对此文意的改写，因此为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【答非所问】A 捕鱼技术迅速提高了 ：选项所说的是数据保守的原因，而非含义，为错误选项，故排除。

【反向干扰】B 那时的捕鱼规模实际上比记录的小：3段4句明确指出“实际捕鱼量要比我们记录的多得多”，B选项与此表意相反，为错误选项，故排除。

【望文生义】D 到目前为止所收集到的数据过时了：选项望文生义，将conservative（保守的）曲解为out of date（过时的），故排除。、
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解第三段的逻辑关系。题干问的是“捕鱼技术提高”意味着什么，而不是问“为什么数据保守”或者“技术本身怎么样”。所以我们要找的是技术提升带来的后果，而不是原因或现象本身。

原文第三段提到，沃姆博承认之前关于海洋大型食肉动物减少的数据其实是“保守估计”。接着用“One reason for this”引出原因：捕鱼技术变好了。然后进一步解释——现在能捕到更多鱼，甚至“海里更大比例的生物都被捞上来了”。这里最关键的一句是“That means a higher proportion of what is in the sea is being caught”，也就是说，人类对海洋生物的实际捕捞强度比数据显示的还要严重。

这样一来，海洋里的生物总量（也就是生物量）其实损失得比我们以为的更厉害。选项C说“海洋的生物量遭受了更大的损失”，正好对应这个意思。它不是在重复“技术提高了”这个事实，而是点出了这个事实背后隐藏的生态危机。

再来看其他选项为什么不对。A选项说“捕鱼技术迅速提高了”，这确实是文中提到的内容，但它只是原因，不是题干所问的“这意味着什么”。题目要的是结果，不是事实陈述，所以A属于答非所问。B选项说“当时的捕捞规模比记录的小”，这跟文意完全相反——文章强调的是实际捕捞比记录显示的更严重，而不是更小。D选项说“数据过时了”，但原文并没有质疑数据的时间有效性，而是说数据本身低估了问题的严重性，所以D也不成立。

总结一下，解这类题要抓住“因果链条”：技术提升 → 捕得更多 → 生物量损失比数据显示的更严重。正确答案一定落在这个逻辑的终点，而不是中间某个环节。

questions.stem: Dr. Myers and other researchers hold that_____ .

options.label: A
options.text: people should look for a baseline that can work for a longer time

options.label: B
options.text: fisheries should keep the yields below 50% of the biomass

options.label: C
options.text: the ocean biomass should be restored to its original level

options.label: D
options.text: people should adjust the fishing baseline to the changing situation

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. people should look for a baseline that can work for a longer time

    人们应当寻找一条能在更长时间内起作用的基线

B. fisheries should keep the yields below 50% of the biomass

    渔场应保持鱼产量低于生物量的50%

C. the ocean biomass should be restored to its original level

    海洋生物量应该恢复到原始水平

D. people should adjust the fishing baseline to the changing situation

    人们应该根据变化的形势来调整捕捞基准


【定位及答案】

根据题干关键词Dr. Myers and other researchers定位在4段。本段关键概念是2句的shifting baseline（要注意现在分词作定语的意义），这是海洋科学家们的主张，其意思是“动态基线”。3句和4句又具体指出：人们只注意到相当短的时期内海洋鱼类数量的变化，因此未能察觉海洋里发生的巨大变化，只有当目标物种的生物量大约是初始水平的50%时，渔场才能获得最大化的可持续产量。由此可知，人们应根据海洋中鱼量的变化来调整捕捞基准，以确保海洋渔业资源的可持续发展，D选项是对此的合理推断，故正确。


【错选分析】

【细节干扰】A 人们应当寻找一条能在更长时间内起作用的基线：4段1句只是说“他们所提出的正确基线需要在人们今后的管理中考虑进去”，并没有提到“该基线能够适用多久”以及“是否应寻找适用更久的基线”的问题，因此A选项为错误选项。

【偷换概念】B、C：4段4句说的是渔场要能收获最大值的鱼产量，必须使目标物种的生物量保持在初始水平的50%，可见，它不是低于50% ，也不是恢复到原始水平，因此B、C两个选项错误。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解文章第四段提到的“shifting baseline”（动态基线）这个概念。作者引用了Dr. Myers和其他研究者的观点，指出人们常常只关注最近几十年的渔业数据，误以为这段时间的鱼类数量就是“正常水平”。但实际上，这种“正常”已经远远低于海洋生态原本的状态。

文中进一步解释说，由于人类的记忆和记录时间太短，我们很容易忽略长期的、缓慢发生的生态退化。比如，当某种鱼的数量只剩下原始水平的一半左右时，渔业反而可能达到所谓的“最大可持续产量”——但这并不意味着生态系统是健康的，只是说明在这个已经受损的基础上，还能勉强维持捕捞。

因此，科学家们主张，不能死守一个固定的捕捞标准，而应该意识到环境是在不断变化的，过去的“正常”可能已经是严重退化的结果。正确的做法是根据当前生态状况灵活调整捕捞的基准，而不是盲目沿用近期的数据作为参考。

选项D说“人们应根据变化的情况调整捕捞基准”，正好对应了这种“动态基线”的思路。其他选项要么曲解了原文意思（比如B把50%当作硬性上限），要么提出不切实际的目标（如C要求恢复到原始水平），而A虽然提到“长期有效的基线”，但仍然隐含了“固定不变”的错误前提。只有D真正抓住了作者和研究者想传达的核心观点。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text3
questions.article:
When prehistoric man arrived in new parts of the world , something strange happened to the large animals : they suddenly became extinct . Smaller species survived . The large , slow-growing animals were easy game , and were quickly hunted to extinction . Now something similar could be happening in the oceans .

That the seas are being overfished has been known for years . What researchers such as Ransom Myers and Boris Worm have shown is just how fast things are changing . They have looked at half a century of data from fisheries around the world . Their methods do not attempt to estimate the actual biomass ( the amount of living biological matter ) of fish species in particular parts of the ocean , but rather changes in that biomass over time . According to their latest paper published in Nature, the biomass of large predators ( animals that kill and eat other animals ) in a new fishery is reduced on average by 80% within 15 years of the start of exploitation . In some long-fished areas, it has halved again since then.

Dr. Worm acknowledges that these figures are conservative . One reason for this is that fishing technology has improved . Today 's vessels can find their prey using satellites and sonar , which were not available 50 years ago . That means a higher proportion of what is in the sea is being caught , so the real difference between present and past is likely to be worse than the one recorded by changes in catch sizes . In the early days , too , longlines would have been more saturated with fish . Some individuals would therefore not have been caught , since no baited hooks would have been available to trap them , leading to an underestimate of fish stocks in the past . Furthermore , in the early days of longline fishing , a lot of fish were lost to sharks after they had been hooked . That is no longer a problem , because there are fewer sharks around now .

Dr. Myers and Dr. Worm argue that their work gives a correct baseline , which future management efforts must take into account . They believe the data support an idea current among marine biologists , that of the " shifting baseline ". The notion is that people have failed to detect the massive changes which have happened in the ocean because they have been looking back only a relatively short time into the past . That matters because theory suggests that the maximum sustainable yield that can be cropped from a fishery comes when the biomass of a target species is about 50% of its original levels . Most fisheries are well below that , which is a bad way to do business .
questions.stem: The author seems to be mainly concerned with most fisheries' _____ .
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. management efficiency

    管理效率

B. biomass level

    生物量水平

C. catch-size limits

    捕捞规模的限制

D. technological application

    科学技术的运用


【定位及答案】

文中1段说海洋生物正面临着灭绝的危险。2段介绍一项研究报告中关于渔场生物量减少的情况。3段说研究报告低估了生物量的实际变化。4段指出当生物量维持在原始水平的50%时，渔场可达最大化的可持续性产量。综观全文，作者始终围绕渔场的生物量变化来论述，所以B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【细节干扰】4段1句和3段4句分别提到了management efforts和catch sizes，但文章强调的是调整基准，寻找捕鱼量和总储量之间的平衡，并非重在讲渔场的管理效率以及对捕鱼数量的限制，因此A、C两个选项错误。

【以偏概全】D 科学技术的运用：3段2句作者提到科技是为了说明科技的进步是致使捕鱼量增大的原因其一，而这并非作者讨论的重点，因此D选项亦予以排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是整篇文章讨论的核心话题是什么。要答对，关键不是盯着某一句话，而是得通读全文，看看作者反复在讲什么。

文章开头就提到海洋生物面临灭绝风险，接着引用一份研究报告，说很多渔场的生物量（也就是鱼群的总重量）已经大幅下降。第三段进一步指出，这份报告其实还低估了问题的严重性——实际减少得比数据显示的更厉害。到了第四段，作者又强调：只有当生物量保持在原始水平的一半左右时，渔场才能实现最大可持续捕捞量。你看，从头到尾，作者一直在围绕“生物量”这个概念展开分析，无论是谈问题、谈数据偏差，还是谈解决方案，都离不开它。

其他选项乍看好像也沾点边。比如A项“管理效率”，文章确实提到了管理措施，但那只是辅助说明，并非主线；C项“捕捞规模限制”也只是在讨论如何维持生物量时顺带提到的手段；D项“科技应用”更是几乎没怎么出现。这些选项要么是一笔带过，要么根本没重点讲，属于典型的“用细节干扰你抓主线”。

所以，真正贯穿全文、支撑作者观点的关键词就是生物量水平，选B才最准确。记住：考研阅读里，正确答案往往不是某个具体做法或工具，而是文章反复强调的那个核心概念。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text4
questions.article:
Many things make people think artists are weird . But the weirdest may be this : artists ' only job is to explore emotions , and yet they choose to focus on the ones that feel bad .

This wasn't always so . The earliest forms of art , like painting and music , are those best suited for expressing joy . But somewhere from the 19th century onward , more artists began seeing happiness as meaningless , phony or , worst of all , boring , as we went from Wordsworth 's daffodils to Baudelaire 's flowers of evil .

You could argue that art became more skeptical of happiness because modern times have seen so much misery . But it 's not as if earlier times didn't know perpetual war , disaster and the massacre of innocents . The reason , in fact , may be just the opposite : there is too much damn happiness in the world today .

After all , what is the one modern form of expression almost completely dedicated to depicting happiness Advertising . The rise of anti-happy art almost exactly tracks the emergence of mass media , and with it , a commercial culture in which happiness is not just an ideal but an ideology .

People in earlier eras were surrounded by reminders of misery . They worked until exhausted , lived with few protections and died young . In the West , before mass communication and literacy , the most powerful mass medium was the church , which reminded worshippers that their souls were in danger and that they would someday be meat for worms . Given all this , they did not exactly need their art to be a bummer too .

Today the messages the average Westerner is surrounded with are not religious but commercial , and forever happy . Fast-food eaters , news anchors , text messengers , all smiling , smiling , smiling . Our magazines feature beaming celebrities and happy families in perfect homes . And since these messages have an agenda — to lure us to open our wallets — they make the very idea of happiness seem unreliable . " Celebrate !" commanded the ads for the arthritis drug Celebrex , before we found out it could increase the risk of heart attacks .

But what we forget — what our economy depends on us forgetting — is that happiness is more than pleasure without pain . The things that bring the greatest joy carry the greatest potential for loss and disappointment . Today , surrounded by promises of easy happiness , we need art to tell us , as religion once did , Memento mori : remember that you will die , that everything ends , and that happiness comes not in denying this but in living with it . It's a message even more bitter than a clove cigarette , yet , somehow , a breath of fresh air .
questions.stem: By citing the examples of poets Wordsworth and Baudelaire, the author intends to show that_____.

options.label: A
options.text: poetry is not as expressive of joy as painting or music

options.label: B
options.text: art grows out of both positive and negative feelings

options.label: C
options.text: poets today are less skeptical of happiness

options.label: D
options.text: artists have changed their focus of interest

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. poetry is not as expressive of joy as painting or music

    诗不像绘画或音乐那样丰富地表达快乐

B. art grows out of both positive and negative feelings

    艺术既产生于正面情感又产生于负面情感

C.poets today are less skeptical of happiness

    如今的诗人对快乐的怀疑变少了

D. artists have changed their focus of interest

    艺术家已改变了他们的兴趣点


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Wordsworth和Baudelaire可定位到原文2段。思路一：2段开头的“This wasn't always so”说明1、2两段之间存在强烈的转折关系，1段说艺术家比较怪异的一个方面是他们喜欢关注负面情感,2段作者指出，事实并非一直是这样。 最早诸如绘画和音乐这些艺术形式都是来表现快乐的，但是从19世纪开始很多艺术家们开始认为幸福是毫无意义的等等，华兹华斯的《水仙花》和波德莱尔的《恶之花》就证明了这种变化。显而易见，作者用这两个例子是为了说明快乐不再是他们表现的主题，他们的重心已然发生了变化，故D选项正确。思路二：2段3句中引导状语从句的as是典型的表示举例的语段特征词，其后是例子，其前是例子所支持的观点，也就是说“But somewhere from the 19th century onward, more artists began seeing happiness as meaning-less……”，是作者讨论的重点；该部分重点强调“越来越多的艺术家们开始把快乐看作是无意义的……”，说明艺术家们由最初的关注快乐转向关注不快乐，他们的关注点发生了变化，D选项是对此的合理推断，故正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 诗不像绘画或音乐那样丰富地表达快乐：选项源自2段2句，该句只是列举了绘画和音乐这两种适于表达快乐的艺术形式，并未将它们与诗歌这种艺术形式作比较，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 艺术既产生于正面情感又产生于负面情感：由2段2、3句可知,艺术是用来表达情感的，并不是产生于情感；且B选项将“两种情感之间的转变”偷换成“既产生于正面情感又产生于负面情感”，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 如今的诗人对快乐的怀疑变少了：由2段3句可知，艺术家对快乐的怀疑变多了，而非C选项所说的越来越少与原文内容相悖，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解作者举华兹华斯和波德莱尔这两个例子到底想说明什么。很多同学一看到人名就慌，其实不用怕——作者提到他们，不是为了讲这两个人本身，而是用他们的作品来证明一个更大的观点。

我们往前看，文章第一段说，现在的艺术家好像特别偏爱痛苦、悲伤这些负面情绪，反而不太愿意表现快乐。但第二段开头马上来了一句“过去可不是这样的”（This wasn’t always so），这就提示我们：情况发生了变化。接着作者解释，在19世纪以前，像绘画、音乐这类艺术形式，本来是用来表达喜悦和美好的；可从19世纪开始，越来越多的艺术家觉得“快乐太肤浅”“没意思”，转而迷上了阴暗、忧郁甚至丑陋的主题。

这时候，作者才举了华兹华斯的《水仙花》和波德莱尔的《恶之花》。注意，《水仙花》其实还带着一点对自然之美的欣喜，而《恶之花》干脆把“恶”和“丑”当作审美对象——这两个例子放在一起，恰恰展示了艺术家关注点的转移：从歌颂快乐，慢慢转向挖掘痛苦与复杂人性。

所以，正确答案要能概括这种“重心转移”的趋势。选项D说“艺术家已经改变了他们的兴趣焦点”，正好对应这个意思。其他选项要么曲解原文（比如A说诗歌不如绘画表达快乐，文中根本没比较艺术形式之间的表达力），要么偷换概念（比如C说现在诗人不怀疑快乐了，实际上文中说的是他们更怀疑了）。只有D准确抓住了作者通过这两个例子想传达的核心变化。

questions.stem: The word“bummer”(Line 6, Para5)most probably means something_____ .
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A.Religious     宗教的

B.unpleasant    令人不愉快的

C.entertaining    令人愉快的

D.commercial     商业的


【定位及答案】

题干已定位至第5段。5段4句的Given all this和句末的too，说明该句与5段前三句之间存在因果关系。5段前三句说的是“人们生活在痛苦之中”，而5段4句又说道“鉴于此，人们不再需要艺术也是一种bummer”，因此，bummer应含有不幸或痛苦之意，因此B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【词汇干扰】A、D两个选项是利用6段1句中的religious but commercial词汇设置的干扰项,故排除。

【反向干扰】C 令人愉快的：依据上述对正确选项的分析可知，C选项为反向干扰，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解文中“bummer”这个词在具体语境中的含义。题干已经明确指向第五段，所以我们重点看这一段的内容。

第五段开头几句话讲的是：人们正经历各种痛苦——失业、焦虑、孤独等等。紧接着第四句说：“Given all this... it’s a bummer that we don’t need art anymore.” 这里的“Given all this”意思是“考虑到以上这些情况”，也就是说，前面提到的种种苦难构成了一个大背景。而作者接着感叹“我们不再需要艺术了，这真是个bummer”。从逻辑上讲，如果人们已经很苦了，却连艺术这种慰藉都没有了，那当然是一件更让人难受的事。所以，“bummer”在这里表达的是一种令人沮丧、不幸或不愉快的情绪。

再来看选项，B项“unpleasant（令人不愉快的）”正好契合这个意思。其他几个选项就不太对劲了。比如A项“religious（宗教的）”和D项“commercial（商业的）”，其实是在下一段才出现的词，跟“bummer”完全没关系，属于典型的张冠李戴。而C项“entertaining（令人愉快的）”更是反着来的——如果“bummer”是开心的事，那作者就不会用它来表达惋惜了。

所以，结合上下文的情感基调和逻辑关系，最合理的答案就是B。

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. emerges in the wake of the anti-happy art

    是随着反快乐艺术而出现的

B. is a cause of disappointment for the general public

    是普通公众失望的一个原因

    取代教堂作为主要的信息来源

    创造了快乐的错觉，而不是快乐本身


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的关键词advertising定位到4段、6段和7段。4段1、2句指出广告是现代描写快乐的表达方式；6段4句指出，商业文化（广告）传递的信息目的是诱惑我们进行消费，而这会使快乐本身显得虚假，5句以举例的形式表明广告只是宣传快乐，并未提示危险；7段1、2句指出真正的快乐是与痛苦和失望相伴的；由此可知，广告中所表现的快乐是不真实的，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 是随着反快乐艺术而出现的：4段3句说：反快乐艺术出现在大众媒体（广告）之后，而A选项的意思是“广告出现在反快乐艺术之后”，两者意思相反，故排除。

【词汇干扰】B 是普通公众失望的一个原因：原文7段2句只是说有可能( potential）会带来失望，故排除。

【过度推理】C 取代教堂作为主要的信息来源：6段1句提到今天西方人被商业广告的信息所包围，但我们不能得出结论说广告是“主要的信息来源”，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是广告在文中被如何描述，关键是要抓住作者对广告“快乐”表达的真实态度。我们不能只看表面，而要结合上下文理解作者的潜台词。

文章第四段开头就说，广告是当代社会描绘快乐的主要方式。听起来好像挺正面？但别急，接着往下看。第六段明确指出，商业文化（包括广告）传递的信息其实是为了“引诱我们消费”，而且这种快乐的呈现方式会让真正的快乐显得“虚假”。后面还举了个例子：广告只展示快乐的一面，却刻意回避了可能存在的风险或代价。这就说明，广告里的快乐是有选择性、经过美化的。

更关键的是第七段，作者强调：真正的快乐从来不是孤立存在的，它总是和痛苦、失望交织在一起。而广告恰恰把快乐包装成一种轻松、无痛、随手可得的东西——这显然和现实不符。所以，广告并没有带来真实的快乐，而是制造了一种“看起来很快乐”的假象。

选项D说“创造了快乐的错觉，而不是快乐本身”，正好对应这个意思。其他选项呢？A提到“反快乐艺术之后出现”，但文中没说广告是在那之后兴起的；B说让公众失望，但失望的是对快乐的理解偏差，不是广告本身导致公众失望；C说取代教堂成为信息源，这完全是无中生有。只有D准确抓住了作者批判广告“虚假快乐”的核心观点。

questions.title: 2006年 阅读Text4
questions.article:
Many things make people think artists are weird . But the weirdest may be this : artists ' only job is to explore emotions , and yet they choose to focus on the ones that feel bad .

This wasn't always so . The earliest forms of art , like painting and music , are those best suited for expressing joy . But somewhere from the 19th century onward , more artists began seeing happiness as meaningless , phony or , worst of all , boring , as we went from Wordsworth 's daffodils to Baudelaire 's flowers of evil .

You could argue that art became more skeptical of happiness because modern times have seen so much misery . But it 's not as if earlier times didn't know perpetual war , disaster and the massacre of innocents . The reason , in fact , may be just the opposite : there is too much damn happiness in the world today .

After all , what is the one modern form of expression almost completely dedicated to depicting happiness Advertising . The rise of anti-happy art almost exactly tracks the emergence of mass media , and with it , a commercial culture in which happiness is not just an ideal but an ideology .

People in earlier eras were surrounded by reminders of misery . They worked until exhausted , lived with few protections and died young . In the West , before mass communication and literacy , the most powerful mass medium was the church , which reminded worshippers that their souls were in danger and that they would someday be meat for worms . Given all this , they did not exactly need their art to be a bummer too .

Today the messages the average Westerner is surrounded with are not religious but commercial , and forever happy . Fast-food eaters , news anchors , text messengers , all smiling , smiling , smiling . Our magazines feature beaming celebrities and happy families in perfect homes . And since these messages have an agenda — to lure us to open our wallets — they make the very idea of happiness seem unreliable . " Celebrate !" commanded the ads for the arthritis drug Celebrex , before we found out it could increase the risk of heart attacks .

But what we forget — what our economy depends on us forgetting — is that happiness is more than pleasure without pain . The things that bring the greatest joy carry the greatest potential for loss and disappointment . Today , surrounded by promises of easy happiness , we need art to tell us , as religion once did , Memento mori : remember that you will die , that everything ends , and that happiness comes not in denying this but in living with it . It's a message even more bitter than a clove cigarette , yet , somehow , a breath of fresh air .
questions.stem: We can learn from the last paragraph that the author believes______ .

options.label: A
options.text: happiness more often than not ends in sadness

options.label: B
options.text: the anti-happy art is distasteful but refreshing

options.label: C
options.text: misery should be enjoyed rather than denied

options.label: D
options.text: the anti-happy art flourishes when economy booms

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. happiness more often than not ends in sadness

    快乐多数情况下以悲伤告终

B. the anti-happy art is distasteful but refreshing

    反快乐艺术令人反感，却使人精神振奋

C. misery should be enjoyed rather than denied

    痛苦应该被享受而不是被否定

D. the anti-happy art flourishes when economy booms

    当经济繁荣时,反快乐艺术也兴盛起来


【定位及答案】

题干已经定位在最后7段。7段4句指出：这一启示甚至比丁香香烟还要苦,但却不知怎么地带来了一股清新的气息，这里说的启示就是用艺术来告诉我们：幸福不会因为否定痛苦而到来，而是应接受生活中的不快（7段3句），这样的艺术就是反快乐艺术（anti-happy art），我们在快乐时也要关注不快乐，这虽然使人痛苦，却是理智与清醒的一种体现。原文中的more better对应B选项的distasteful，原文中的a breath of fresh air对应B选项的refreshing，故B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【细节干扰】A 快乐多数情况下以悲伤告终：原文7段3句讲到：一切都会结束，那么自然所有的快乐也都会结束，但其以哪种状态结束，原文并没有提及，故排除。

【偷换概念】C 痛苦应该被享受而不是被否定：原文7段3句后半部分指出：幸福会与那些时刻提醒人们悲伤仍旧存在的信息共存，其中living with it中的it指代you will die，everything ends等，可见，幸福不会因否定痛苦而到来，我们必须接受或忍受痛苦，但“接受”并不等于“享受（enjoyed）”，因此C选项错误。

【偷换概念】D 当经济繁荣时,反快乐艺术也兴盛起来：原文7段1句提到经济时，意在表述经济是依赖于盲目的快乐这层含义，而D选项表达的却是经济对反快乐艺术的正向影响，二者表达含义完全不同，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解作者对“反快乐艺术”（anti-happy art）的真实态度。很多同学一看到“反快乐”就以为作者在批评它，其实恰恰相反——作者是带着欣赏的眼光来看待这种艺术的。

文章倒数第二段提到，这种艺术带来的启示“比丁香香烟还要苦”，说明它确实让人不舒服、不好受，甚至有点“难以下咽”。但紧接着作者话锋一转，说它“不知怎么地带来了一股清新的气息”（a breath of fresh air）。这个表达很关键——“清新空气”在英语里通常代表一种令人精神一振、豁然开朗的感觉。也就是说，虽然这种艺术让人难受，但它能唤醒我们，让我们更清醒、更真实地面对生活。

现在看选项，B 项说“反快乐艺术令人反感，却使人精神振奋”，正好对应了原文中“苦”和“清新空气”这两个看似矛盾实则统一的感受。“令人反感”对应它的苦涩和不适，“精神振奋”则呼应那股“清新的气息”。所以 B 是正确答案。

其他选项为什么不对？A 项说“快乐大多以悲伤告终”，这是对原文的过度引申，文章没讨论快乐的结局，而是强调不能回避痛苦；C 项说“应该享受痛苦”，这太极端了，作者只是说要“承认”或“接受”痛苦，而不是去“享受”它；D 项把反快乐艺术和经济繁荣挂钩，但原文根本没提经济状况，纯属无中生有。

记住：考研阅读里，作者的态度往往藏在转折词之后。像“but”“yet”“however”后面的话，常常才是重点。

questions.stem: which of the following is TRUE of the text?

options.label: A
options.text: Religion once functioned as a reminder of misery

options.label: B
options.text: Art provides a balance between expectation and reality

options.label: C
options.text: People feel disappointed at the realities of modern society

options.label: D
options.text: Mass media are inclined to cover disasters and deaths

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. Religion once functioned as a reminder of misery.

    宗教曾经作为痛苦的提醒物 

B. Art provides a balance between expectation and reality.

    艺术使期望与现实平衡

C. People feel disappointed at the realities of modern society.

    人们对现代社会的现实感到失望

D. Mass media are inclined to cover disasters and deaths.

    大众传媒往往会报道灾难和死亡


【定位及答案】

题干没有提供定位信息，只能根据选项定位。A选项的关键词： Religion, reminder, misery和5段1、3句的reminders of misery（痛苦的提醒物），church（教堂），reminded（提醒）等对应。5段3句指出，在西方，在大众传媒和教育普及之前，最有影响力的大众媒介是教堂，它提醒信徒们，他们的灵魂处于危险之中，他们总有一天会成为蛆虫的食物，由此可见，A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】本文意在说明：反快乐艺术的作用是提醒人们快乐的背后可能存在着痛苦，文章并未提到艺术的平衡作用以及人们对现实的不满，故排除B、C两个选项。

【反向干扰】D 大众传媒往往会报道灾难和死亡：由6段可知，大众传媒使快乐显得虚假，它只宣传快乐，并不提醒我们潜在的危险，可见大众传媒不是报道灾难和死亡，而是宣扬虚假的幸福，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于理解文章第五段的核心意思，而不是靠题干直接定位。因为题干没给具体线索，所以我们得从选项入手，看看哪个选项能和原文内容真正对得上。

先看A选项：“宗教曾经作为痛苦的提醒物”。乍一听有点抽象，但回到原文第五段，作者确实提到，在大众传媒和现代教育还没普及的年代，教堂是当时最有影响力的“大众媒体”。它干了啥？不是给人打鸡血，而是不断提醒信徒：你们的灵魂有危险，终有一天会变成蛆虫的食物。这种说法虽然听起来吓人，但本质上就是在强调人生的苦难和死亡的必然——也就是在“提醒人们世间的痛苦”。所以A选项其实准确概括了这段的意思。

再来看其他几个选项为什么不对。B选项说“艺术平衡期望与现实”，但整篇文章根本没讨论艺术的作用，属于无中生有；C选项讲“人们对现代社会失望”，虽然文章提到了现代人面对大量负面新闻可能感到焦虑，但并没有说大家因此对社会整体失望，这个结论过度引申了；D选项说“大众媒体爱报道灾难和死亡”，这倒是文中提到的现象，但它只是用来和过去的宗教做对比的背景信息，并不是作者要表达的主要观点，更不是第40题所问的核心内容。

说到底，这道题考的是你能不能抓住段落的主旨，而不是被表面细节带偏。A选项虽然用词简略，却精准对应了原文中宗教在过去所扮演的角色——不是安慰剂，而是一面照出人生残酷真相的镜子。

questions.title: 2007年 阅读Text1
questions.article:
If you were to examine the birth certificates of every soccer player in 2006’s World Cup tournament , you would most likely find a noteworthy quirk : elite soccer players are more likely to have been born in the earlier months of the year than in the later months . If you then examined the European national youth teams that feed the World Cup and professional ranks , you would find this strange phenomenon to be even more pronounced .

What might account for this strange phenomenon Here are a few guesses ：a) certain astrological signs confer superior soccer skills ; b) winter-born babies tend to have higher oxygen capacity , which increases soccer stamina ; c) soccer-mad parents are more likely to conceive children in springtime , at the annual peak of soccer mania ; d) none of the above .

Anders Ericsson , a 58-year-old psychology professor at Florida State University , says he believes strongly in “ none of the above .” Ericsson grew up in Sweden , and studied nuclear engineering until he realized he would have more opportunity to conduct his own research if he switched to psychology . His first experiment , nearly 30 years ago , involved memory : training a person to hear and then repeat a random series of numbers . “ With the first subject , after about 20 hours of training , his digit span had risen from 7 to 20 , ” Ericsson recalls . “ He kept improving , and after about 200 hours of training he had risen to over 80 numbers .”

This success , coupled with later research showing that memory itself is not genetically determined , led Ericsson to conclude that the act of memorizing is more of a cognitive exercise than an intuitive one . In other words , whatever inborn differences two people may exhibit in their abilities to memorize , those differences are swamped by how well each person “ encodes ” the information . And the best way to learn how to encode information meaningfully , Ericsson determined , was a process known as deliberate practice . Deliberate practice entails more than simply repeating a task . Rather , it involves setting specific goals , obtaining immediate feedback and concentrating as much on technique as on outcome .

Ericsson and his colleagues have thus taken to studying expert performers in a wide range of pursuits , including soccer . They gather all the data they can , not just performance statistics and biographical details but also the results of their own laboratory experiments with high achievers . Their work makes a rather startling assertion : the trait we commonly call talent is highly overrated . Or , put another way, expert performers — whether in memory or surgery , ballet or computer programming — are nearly always made , not born .
questions.stem: The birthday phenomenon found among soccer players is mentioned to______ .

options.label: A
options.text: stress the importance of professional training

options.label: B
options.text: spotlight the soccer superstars in the World Cup

options.label: C
options.text: introduce the topic of what makes expert performance

options.label: D
options.text: explain why some soccer teams play better than others

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. stress the importance of professional training

   强调专业训练的重要性

B. spotlight the soccer superstars in the World Cup

   突出世界杯中的超级球星

C. introduce the topic of what makes expert performance

   引出“如何造就出色表现”这一话题

D.explain why some soccer teams play better than others

   解释为什么有些球队踢得比别的球队好


【定位及答案】

题目中的birthday phenomenon指的是1段中提到的“出色的足球运动员更可能在一年的前几个月份中出生”这一现象。1段先后给出了两个例子，2段引出了以设问结构为特征的讨论话题，即“What might account for this strange phenomenon?”（注意该句中的this strange phenomenon指代一段讨论的“出色的足球运动员出生在前半年”这一现象）。而文章接下来的3段不再描述这些猜测，而是通过分析心理学家埃里克森的研究及结果，探讨表现出色的因素。可见首段是作为引子引出话题的，因此C选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 强调专业训练的重要性 ：作者在将在3段3、4句强调了专业训练的重要性，其目的是为了说明专业训练是导致出色表现的根本因素这一主题，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 突出世界杯中的超级球星：作者关注的是如何造就出色表现的原因，并非为了突出某一明星，故排除。

【无中生有】D 解释为什么有些球队踢得比别的球队好：文中比较的是球员，并未提及任何球队的比较，且这也不符文中含义，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是文章开头提到的“生日现象”（birthday phenomenon）有什么作用。其实，作者并不是真的要研究出生月份和踢球水平之间的神秘联系，而是用这个看似奇怪的现象来吸引读者注意，引出一个更深层的问题：到底是什么造就了顶尖的表现？

你看第一段先讲了一个有趣的现象——很多优秀足球运动员都出生在一年的前几个月；第二段马上抛出一个问题：“这到底是为什么？”紧接着，文章从第三段开始就不再纠结于出生时间了，而是转向介绍心理学家埃里克森的研究，重点讨论“刻意练习”和专业训练如何真正决定一个人能否成为高手。这说明，前面的“生日现象”只是一个引子，真正的主题是探讨专家级表现背后的成因。

所以正确选项应该是C，“引出‘什么造就了出色表现’这一话题”。其他选项虽然看起来有点相关，但都不是开头这段的主要目的。比如A选项说“强调专业训练的重要性”，这确实是后文的重点，但不是第一段的作用；B选项聚焦球星，D选项比较球队强弱，都偏离了文章真正想讨论的核心问题。

简单来说，考研英语阅读里经常用一个有趣的现象或故事开头，但它的任务不是讲故事本身，而是为全文的主题做铺垫。抓住这一点，就能避免被细节带偏，准确判断作者的写作意图。

They gather all the data they can , not just performance statistics and biographical details but also the results of their own laboratory experiments with high achievers . Their work makes a rather startling assertion : the trait we commonly call talent is highly overrated . Or , put another way, expert performers — whether in memory or surgery , ballet or computer programming — are nearly always made , not born .
questions.stem: The word “mania”(Line 5, Paragraph 2) most probably means______ .
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A.fun    乐趣

B.craze    狂热

C. Hysteria    歇斯底里

D. excitement    兴奋


【定位及答案】

mania一词不是考研英语大纲词汇，因此，需要根据上下文推测其含义。从文中2段2句中soccer-mad parents（特别喜爱足球的父母）可推测出，他们更容易在一年中足球最狂热的季节孕育子女，mad与B选项中的craze为同义替换，所以选B选项。


【定位及答案】

【偷换概念】A 乐趣：根据上述分析可知，2段2句主要表达的意思是，父母对于足球的热爱可能会促使父母喜欢在春季孕育子女，A选项的fun（乐趣）与原文意思不符，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 歇斯底里：选项的hysteria（敬斯底里）多含贬义色彩，而文章只是在客观描述父母对足球的喜爱，故排除C选项；

【词汇干扰】D 兴奋：excitement和mania意思相近，但语气上不如craze强烈，而且excitement只强调暂时的兴奋状态，不是最佳选项，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题考查的是对生词 mania 含义的推测能力。这个词虽然不在考研大纲里，但别慌，我们完全可以通过上下文来判断它的意思。

回到原文第二段第二句，里面提到 “soccer-mad parents” —— 这里的 “mad” 并不是“发疯”的意思，而是英语中常见的表达，表示“极度热爱”或“痴迷”。比如我们说 someone is mad about music，就是说这个人超级喜欢音乐。所以，“soccer-mad parents” 指的就是那些对足球特别着迷的父母。

接下来句子说，这些父母更可能在一年中足球最“mania”的季节怀上孩子。显然，这里的 mania 要和前面的 “mad” 呼应，表达一种强烈的热情或狂热状态。四个选项中，craze 正好就是“狂热、风靡”的意思，和上下文的情绪强度完全匹配。

再来看其他选项为什么不对：A 选项 fun（乐趣）太轻了，只是普通的开心，远达不到“mad”那种程度；C 选项 hysteria（歇斯底里）带有明显的负面情绪，通常指失控的恐慌或情绪爆发，而原文只是客观描述球迷的热情，并没有贬义；D 选项 excitement（兴奋）虽然也正面，但它强调的是一时的情绪高涨，比如看比赛时的激动，而 craze 更强调一种持续的、群体性的痴迷状态，更贴合“足球狂热季”这个语境。

所以，综合来看，B 选项 craze 是最准确、最符合原文语气的答案。

questions.title: 2007年 阅读Text1
questions.article:
If you were to examine the birth certificates of every soccer player in 2006’s World Cup tournament , you would most likely find a noteworthy quirk : elite soccer players are more likely to have been born in the earlier months of the year than in the later months . If you then examined the European national youth teams that feed the World Cup and professional ranks , you would find this strange phenomenon to be even more pronounced .

What might account for this strange phenomenon Here are a few guesses ：a) certain astrological signs confer superior soccer skills ; b) winter-born babies tend to have higher oxygen capacity , which increases soccer stamina ; c) soccer-mad parents are more likely to conceive children in springtime , at the annual peak of soccer mania ; d) none of the above .

Anders Ericsson , a 58-year-old psychology professor at Florida State University , says he believes strongly in “ none of the above .” Ericsson grew up in Sweden , and studied nuclear engineering until he realized he would have more opportunity to conduct his own research if he switched to psychology . His first experiment , nearly 30 years ago , involved memory : training a person to hear and then repeat a random series of numbers . “ With the first subject , after about 20 hours of training , his digit span had risen from 7 to 20 , ” Ericsson recalls . “ He kept improving , and after about 200 hours of training he had risen to over 80 numbers .”

This success , coupled with later research showing that memory itself is not genetically determined , led Ericsson to conclude that the act of memorizing is more of a cognitive exercise than an intuitive one . In other words , whatever inborn differences two people may exhibit in their abilities to memorize , those differences are swamped by how well each person “ encodes ” the information . And the best way to learn how to encode information meaningfully , Ericsson determined , was a process known as deliberate practice . Deliberate practice entails more than simply repeating a task . Rather , it involves setting specific goals , obtaining immediate feedback and concentrating as much on technique as on outcome .

Ericsson and his colleagues have thus taken to studying expert performers in a wide range of pursuits , including soccer . They gather all the data they can , not just performance statistics and biographical details but also the results of their own laboratory experiments with high achievers . Their work makes a rather startling assertion : the trait we commonly call talent is highly overrated . Or , put another way, expert performers — whether in memory or surgery , ballet or computer programming — are nearly always made , not born .
questions.stem: According to Ericsson , good memory_____.

options.label: A
options.text: depends on meaningful processing of information

options.label: B
options.text: results from intuitive rather than cognitive exercises

options.label: C
options.text: is determined by genetic rather than psychological factors

options.label: D
options.text: requires immediate feedback and a high degree of concentration

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. depends on meaningful processing of information 

    依赖于对信息进行有意义的加工

B. results from intuitive rather than cognitive exercises

    来自于直觉活动而不是认知活

C. is determined by genetic rather than psychological factors

    取决于基因遗传而不是心理因素

D.requires immediate feedback and a high degree of concentration

    需要及时的反馈和高度集中的注意力


【定位及答案】

由题目中的关键词Ericsson和good memory可知，答案应定位在3段的最后3句和4段。文章3段提到了有关记忆的实验，4段介绍了埃里克森有关记忆的结论：记忆是一个认知过程，而非直觉活动；先天的记忆差异会被个人对信息的“编码”能力所掩盖；记忆是“刻意训练”，它包括制定具体目标、获得及时反馈以及注重结果和技巧方法。这说明，埃里克森认为，好的记忆力依赖于人们对信息的有效整合。A选项中的meaningful processing of information是对原文4段2句中“encodes”the information的同义转述，所以A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】B、C 两个选项是对原文的反向干扰，文章4段1句说埃里克森认为良好的记忆力是一个认知过程,可以通过后天的心理认知练习培养，而不是直觉活动，也不是由先天基因决定的，故排除。

【张冠李戴】D 需要及时的反馈和高度集中的注意力：选项是在解释“刻意训练”，与题意不符，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是Ericsson（埃里克森）认为“好的记忆力”是怎么来的。要答对这道题，关键不是靠猜，而是回到原文找他说了什么。

文章第三段后半部分和第四段集中讲了Ericsson的观点。他通过实验发现，那些看起来记忆力超群的人，并不是天生脑子就比别人好，而是因为他们会用一套特别的方法去处理信息。比如，他们会把零散的信息组织成有意义的组块，或者跟自己已有的知识联系起来——这个过程在心理学里就叫“编码”（encoding）。

更重要的是，Ericsson强调，这种能力不是靠直觉或者天赋，而是通过**刻意练习**练出来的。刻意练习有几个特点：有明确目标、能及时得到反馈、不断调整方法。但注意，题目问的是“好的记忆力依赖于什么”，而不是“怎么练出来”。所以我们要抓住最核心的一点：**记忆好坏的关键，在于你如何加工信息**。

现在看选项，A说“依赖于对信息进行有意义的加工”，这正好对应原文说的“编码”过程——也就是把信息变得有结构、有联系、有意义。而B说“来自直觉而非认知”，这直接和Ericsson的观点相反，他明确说记忆是认知过程，不是直觉。C提到“基因决定”，但原文恰恰说先天差异会被后天的编码能力“掩盖”，说明心理因素更重要。D虽然提到了“及时反馈”和“专注”，但这只是刻意练习的条件，不是记忆力本身的决定因素，属于偷换概念。

所以，正确答案是A，因为它准确抓住了Ericsson理论的核心：好记性不是天生的，而是看你有没有把信息“加工”得有意义。

questions.stem: Ericsson and his colleagues believe that___ .

options.label: A
options.text: talent is a dominating factor for professional success

options.label: B
options.text: biographical data provide the key to excellent performance

options.label: C
options.text: the role of talent tends to be overlooked

options.label: D
options.text: high achievers owe their success mostly to nurture

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. talent is a dominating factor for professional success

    天赋是职业成功的决定因素

B. biographical data provide the key to excel-lent performance

    生平资料是卓越表现的关键

C. the role of talent tends to be overlooked

    天赋的作用往往被忽视

D. high achievers owe their success mostly to nurture

    高成就者将他们的成功归功于后天的培养


【定位及答案】

根据题目中的关键词Ericsson and his colleague，可知答案在最后一段。该段最后一句为文章主旨，点明成功人士的成功在于后天的培养。D选项中high achievers与原文5段4句中expert performers意义相同，owe their success mostly to nurture是对4句中are nearly always made的同义转述，所以答案选D选项。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 天赋是职业成功的决定因素：选项与5段4句所述相悖，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 生平资料是卓越表现的关键：收集生平资料是对优秀人士进行研究的一种方法，并不能由此推断出生平资料是卓越表现的关键，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 天赋的作用往往被忽视：由5段3句可知，人们Overrated（高估）而非overlooked（忽视）了天赋的作用，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是Ericsson和他的同事对“高成就者成功原因”的看法。要解答它，关键得回到文章最后一段去找线索。作者在那一段明确指出，那些在各自领域表现卓越的人，并不是因为天生就比别人强，而是通过长期、系统的训练和后天努力才达到顶尖水平的。

特别注意最后一句话：“专家级的表现几乎总是被‘培养’出来的（are nearly always made）”，这句话直接否定了“天赋决定论”，强调了后天环境和训练的核心作用。选项D说“高成就者将他们的成功主要归功于后天培养”，正好对应这个意思——“owe their success mostly to nurture”就是对“are nearly always made”的通俗表达。

其他几个选项为什么不对呢？A说天赋是决定因素，这跟原文观点完全相反；B提到生平资料是关键，但文章根本没把“biographical data”当作重点；C说天赋被忽视了，可原文压根没讨论“是否被忽视”，而是直接质疑天赋本身的作用。所以只有D准确传达了作者和Ericsson的核心立场。

questions.stem: Which of the following proverbs is closest to the message the text tries to convey？
questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A.“Faith will move mountains.”

“精诚所至，金石为开。”

B.“One reaps what one sows.”

“种瓜得瓜,种豆得豆。”

C.“Practice makes perfect.”

“熟能生巧。”

D."Like father, like son."

“有其父，必有其子。”


【定位及答案】

解答本题时，一方面要把握全文的意思，另方一面还要理解各选项中谚语的意思。如前所述，本文通过出色的足球运动员的出生时间这一特别现象引出心理学家埃里克森的研究成果，说明成功人士不是天生的，而是后天培养的。C选项中的practice（后天训练）是达到perfect的前提条件。因此正确答案为C选项。


【错选分析】

【以偏概全】A 精诚所至，金石为开：选项是针对“加强训练可提高记忆力”这一事例而说的，并非全文主旨，故排除。

【无中生有】B 种瓜得瓜,种豆得豆：选项在文中并未提及，故排除。

【以偏概全】D 有其父，必有其子：选项是2段2句中强调的遗传作用，但是作者在后文3段1句已经否定了该说法并非全文主旨。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于抓住文章的中心思想，而不是被某个细节带偏。整篇文章讲的是：那些看起来天赋异禀的顶尖足球运动员，其实并不是天生就比别人强，而是因为他们在关键成长期获得了更多训练机会——比如出生月份靠前的孩子，在青少年比赛中更容易被选中，从而得到更多练习和指导。心理学家埃里克森的研究也支持这个观点：真正的专家不是靠天赋，而是靠长期、刻意的练习积累出来的。

现在看四个选项，我们要找一个最能概括“成功来自后天努力”这个核心意思的谚语。“Practice makes perfect”（熟能生巧） 正好表达了这个理念——只有通过反复练习，才能达到卓越。这和文章强调“训练比天赋更重要”的主旨完全吻合。

其他几个选项为什么不对呢？A选项“精诚所至，金石为开”听起来很励志，但它强调的是信念或意志的力量，而文章根本没谈“信心”或“决心”，只谈了实际的训练量，所以不匹配。B选项“种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆”讲的是因果报应或自然规律，但文中并没有讨论行为与结果之间的道德或自然因果关系。D选项“有其父，必有其子”强调遗传或家庭影响，可文章恰恰在反驳这种“天生注定”的观点——作者明确指出，早期优势并非来自基因，而是来自环境和机会，所以这个选项正好和文章立场相反。

说到底，选对答案的关键不是背了多少谚语，而是能不能从全文出发，找到那个真正贴合作者想表达的核心观点的选项。记住：考研阅读考的是整体理解，不是局部细节。

questions.title: 2007年 阅读Text2
questions.article:
For the past several years , the Sunday newspaper supplement Parade has featured a column called “ Ask Marilyn .” People are invited to query Marilyn Vos Savant , who at age 10 had tested at a mental level of someone about 23 years old ; that gave her an IQ of 228 — the highest score ever recorded . IQ tests ask you to complete verbal and visual analogies , to envision paper after it has been folded and cut , and to deduce numerical sequences , among other similar tasks . So it is a bit confusing when Vos Savant fields such queries from the average Joe (whose IQ is 100) as , What ’s the difference between love and fondness Or what is the nature of luck and coincidence It’s not obvious how the capacity to visualize objects and to figure out numerical patterns suits one to answer questions that have eluded some of the best poets and philosophers .

Clearly , intelligence encompasses more than a score on a test . Just what does it mean to be smart How much of intelligence can be specified , and how much can we learn about it from neurology , genetics , computer science and other fields

The defining term of intelligence in humans still seems to be the IQ score , even though IQ tests are not given as often as they used to be . The test comes primarily in two forms: the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale and the Wechsler Intelligence Scales (both come in adult and children’s version). Generally costing several hundred dollars, they are usually given only by psychologists, although variations of them populate bookstores and the World Wide Web . Superhigh scores like Vos Savant ’s are no longer possible , because scoring is now based on a statistical population distribution among age peers , rather than simply dividing the mental age by the chronological age and multiplying by 100 . Other standardized tests , such as the Scholastic Assessment Test ( SAT ) and the Graduate Record Exam ( GRE ), capture the main aspects of IQ tests .

Such standardized tests may not assess all the important elements necessary to succeed in school and in life , argues Robert J. Sternberg . In his article “ How Intelligent Is Intelligence Testing? ”, Sternberg notes that traditional tests best assess analytical and verbal skills but fail to measure creativity and practical knowledge , components also critical to problem solving and life success . Moreover , IQ tests do not necessarily predict so well once populations or situations change . Research has found that IQ predicted leadership skills when the tests were given under low-stress conditions ，but under high-stress conditions ，IQ was negatively correlated with leadership — that is , it predicted the opposite . Anyone who has toiled through SAT will testify that test-taking skill also matters , whether it’s knowing when to guess or what questions to skip .

options.label: B
options.text: Folding or cutting paper into different shapes.

options.label: C
options.text: Telling the differences between certain concepts.

options.label: D

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. Answering philosophical questions.

    回答哲学问题

B. Folding or cutting paper into different shapes.

    把纸折叠或剪裁成不同的形状

C. Telling the differences between certain concepts.

    区分某些概念的不同

D. Choosing words or graphs similar to the given ones.

    根据所给词汇或图片选择近义词或类似图片


【定位及答案】

这是短文的第一个细节问题，应该从短文开头寻找答题信息。根据题干中的关键词required in an intelligence test 定位在1段3句，D选项中words or graphs similar to与原文1段3句中 verbal and visual analogies对应，所以正确答案为D选项。


【错选分析】

【无关干扰】A、C两个选项分别在1段6句和4句提到，但其都不是指智力测试的内容，故都予以排除。

【偷换概念】B 把纸折叠或剪裁成不同的形状：选项强调的是动手能力，而测试中体现的是想象能力，二者分属不同类型的问题，因此B选项错误。
questions.tips:
这道题问的是：智力测试中通常会要求考生做什么？我们要找的不是泛泛而谈的内容，而是文章里明确提到的具体任务。

回到原文第一段，作者在介绍智力测试时举了几个例子。其中一句特别关键：“These tests often require people to complete verbal and visual analogies.” 这句话的意思是，测试经常让人完成语言类和视觉类的类比题。所谓“类比”，就是找出两组事物之间的相似关系——比如“苹果之于水果，正如胡萝卜之于______”，你需要选出“蔬菜”这样的答案。

现在看选项，D 选项说“根据所给词汇或图片选择近义词或类似图片”，虽然用词不完全一样，但本质上就是在描述“类比”这个操作——无论是文字还是图像，都是在找相似或对应的关系。这就和原文的 “verbal and visual analogies” 完全对上了。

简单来说，解这类题的关键就是抓住题干关键词，回原文找原话或同义表达。D 选项虽然换了个说法，但意思最贴近原文，自然就是正确答案。

questions.title: 2007年 阅读Text2
questions.article:
For the past several years , the Sunday newspaper supplement Parade has featured a column called “ Ask Marilyn .” People are invited to query Marilyn Vos Savant , who at age 10 had tested at a mental level of someone about 23 years old ; that gave her an IQ of 228 — the highest score ever recorded . IQ tests ask you to complete verbal and visual analogies , to envision paper after it has been folded and cut , and to deduce numerical sequences , among other similar tasks . So it is a bit confusing when Vos Savant fields such queries from the average Joe (whose IQ is 100) as , What ’s the difference between love and fondness Or what is the nature of luck and coincidence It’s not obvious how the capacity to visualize objects and to figure out numerical patterns suits one to answer questions that have eluded some of the best poets and philosophers .

Clearly , intelligence encompasses more than a score on a test . Just what does it mean to be smart How much of intelligence can be specified , and how much can we learn about it from neurology , genetics , computer science and other fields

The defining term of intelligence in humans still seems to be the IQ score , even though IQ tests are not given as often as they used to be . The test comes primarily in two forms: the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale and the Wechsler Intelligence Scales (both come in adult and children’s version). Generally costing several hundred dollars, they are usually given only by psychologists, although variations of them populate bookstores and the World Wide Web . Superhigh scores like Vos Savant ’s are no longer possible , because scoring is now based on a statistical population distribution among age peers , rather than simply dividing the mental age by the chronological age and multiplying by 100 . Other standardized tests , such as the Scholastic Assessment Test ( SAT ) and the Graduate Record Exam ( GRE ), capture the main aspects of IQ tests .

Such standardized tests may not assess all the important elements necessary to succeed in school and in life , argues Robert J. Sternberg . In his article “ How Intelligent Is Intelligence Testing? ”, Sternberg notes that traditional tests best assess analytical and verbal skills but fail to measure creativity and practical knowledge , components also critical to problem solving and life success . Moreover , IQ tests do not necessarily predict so well once populations or situations change . Research has found that IQ predicted leadership skills when the tests were given under low-stress conditions ，but under high-stress conditions ，IQ was negatively correlated with leadership — that is , it predicted the opposite . Anyone who has toiled through SAT will testify that test-taking skill also matters , whether it’s knowing when to guess or what questions to skip .
questions.stem: What can be inferred about intelligence testing from Paragraph 3？

options.label: A
options.text: People no longer use IQ scores as an indicator of intelligence.

options.label: B
options.text: More versions of IQ tests are now available on the Internet.

options.label: C
options.text: The test contents and formats for adults and children may be different.

options.label: D
options.text: Scientists have defined the important elements of human intelligence.

questions.analysis:
【选项概览】

A. People no longer use IQ scores as an indicator of intelligence.

    人们不再使用智商分数作为智力的标准

B. More versions of IQ tests are now available on the Internet.

    现在互联网上可以获得更多版本的智力测试

C. The test contents and formats for adults and children may be different.

    成人和儿童使用的智力测试的内容和形式可能不同

D. Scientists have defined the important elements of human intelligence.

    科学家已经明确了人类智力中的重要成分


【定位及答案】

3段2句说：智力测试主要有两种形式：……（这两种测量表都分为成人版和儿童版）。阅读时要注意括号中的内容，因为很多考生通常会忽略这些内容，既然是两种版本，就肯定有区别，由此可知答案为C选项。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 人们不再使用智商分数作为智力的标准：3段1句可知，智商仍是智力测试的标准，故排除。

【无关干扰】B 现在互联网上可以获得更多版本的智力测试：选项的more属于无关干扰，3段3句说道“互联网上可以看到智力测试的修订版”，而非B选项中的“more versions（更多版本）”，故排除。

【无中生有】D 科学家已经明确了人类智力中的重要成分：3段中未提及任何有关科学家（scientists）的研究证明和人类智力的成分（elements）问题，故排除。
questions.tips:
这道题的关键在于回到原文第三段找线索。文章提到，目前主流的智力测试主要有两种类型，并且特别用括号补充说明：这两种测试都分别设有成人版和儿童版。这句话看似轻描淡写，其实暗藏玄机——如果只是简单换个名字，没必要专门区分“成人”和“儿童”两个版本；既然特意分开，就说明它们在内容或形式上肯定存在差异。

我们再来看选项。C 选项说“成人和儿童使用的智力测试在内容和形式上可能不同”，这正好和原文的暗示对得上。虽然原文没直接写“内容不同”，但分设版本本身就强烈暗示了这种区别，属于合理推断。

其他几个选项问题就比较明显了。A 选项说“人们不再用智商分数衡量智力”，但全文根本没有否定 IQ 分数的使用，反而一直在讨论如何改进测试，所以这是无中生有。B 选项提到“网上有更多版本的 IQ 测试”，原文压根没提互联网的事，纯属添油加醋。D 选项说“科学家已经明确了智力的重要成分”，可文章恰恰强调智力定义仍有争议，科学家还在探索中，因此这个说法过于绝对，与文意相反。

所以，正确答案是 C。做这类题时，一定要留意原文中那些看似不起眼的细节，比如括号里的补充说明——考研英语最喜欢在这种地方设考点。

questions.article:
